[[Xtreme Dash|Xtreme Dash ν]] (Version 2.0) |WBO=https://worldbeyblade.org/Thread-Product-BX-01-Starter-Dran-Sword-3-60F }}{{Translation|'''DranSword 3-60F'''|ドランソード{{Ruby|3-60|スリーシクスティー}}{{Ruby|F|フラット}}|DoranSōdo Surī Shikusutī Furatto|DranSword Three Sixty Flat}} is an Attack Type Beyblade released by [[Takara Tomy]]. It was released as a Starter in Japan on June 10th, 2023 during the CoroCoro Spirit Festival for 1980円. Its regular retail release in Japan was on July 15th, 2023. It later debuted in western countries as '''Sword Dran 3-60F''' in a Starter Pack released by [[Hasbro]] for USD$9.99 in the United States. DranSword would later get a ''Version 2.0'' release, which released in Japan as a BX-00 Booster on August 8th, 2026 for 1600円. In the anime and manga, it was given to a young [[Jaxon Cross]] as a parting gift from his mentor, [[Ginro]]; it originally had ''Metal Coat: Blue'' paint, although this gradually wore down over years into its current form. [[Khrome Ryugu]] also borrows this Bey for his match at the peak of [[The X]], and later uses a replica bought from a store. DranSword's ''Version 2.0'' release would later debut in the anime/manga series, which would be developed by the [[Bey Kingdom]]. It can be obtained with a [[wikipedia:Mail order|mail order]] postcard included with the February 2024 issue of the [[CoroCoro Comic]] magazine, which released on January 15th, 2024.[https://corocoro.jp/news/377976/ CoroCoro Online Post about HellsScythe 3-80F] The first batch of orders were shipped on January 27th, 2024. The deadline for the mail order was February 17th, 2024.CoroCoro Comic February 2024 Issue, mail order postcard The coloring is based on Team [[Persona]]'s colors and the Gear Chip design is by ''Beyblade X'' manga artist [[wikipedia:Posuka Demizu|Posuka Demizu]]. Included with the Beyblade is a "dress-up" sticker sheet and an illustration card. In the manga, the Beyblade is owned by [[Robin Kazami]], who created it with the help of [[Jaxon Cross]] and [[Multi Nana-iro]]. It is intended to represent the friendship of Team Persona, and contains a part from each of their first Beys when they met.CoroCoro Comic January 2024 Issue, page 40 ==Blade - HellsScythe== {{Part|Blade - HellsScythe}} ==Ratchet - 3-80== {{Part|Ratchet - 3-80}} ==Bit - Flat== {{Part|Bit - Flat}} ==Gallery== ===Toyline=== ====Takara Tomy==== HellsScythe 3-80F.jpg HellsScythe 3-80F Stickers.png ===Anime=== ===Manga=== HellsScythe 3-80F (Manga).jpg SP X Bey completed.jpg|Completed SP X Bey Burst Finish.jpg|[[Burst Finish]] against [[Jaxon Cross|Jaxon]]'s [[DranSword 3-60F]] SP X Bey Spread.jpg|Illustration card spreadCoroCoro Comic February 2024 Issue SP X Bey Gear Chip.jpg|Gear Chip ===Video Game=== Beyblade X App HellsScythe 3-80F.png|[[Beyblade X App]] model. Beyblade X App HellsScythe 3-80F Top View.png|Beyblade X App model, top view. ==Videos== ==Trivia== *The Beyblade incorporates a part from each member of Team Persona: **Robin's [[Blade - HellsScythe|HellsScythe]] Blade from [[HellsScythe 4-60T]]. **Multi's [[Ratchet - 3-80|3-80]] Ratchet from [[KnightShield 3-80N]]. **Jaxon's [[Bit - Flat|Flat]] Bit from [[DranSword 3-60F]]. *On the cover of chapter 8 of the manga, the members of Persona can be seen in a "Bey customization meeting" that resulted in this Bey. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Basic Line Beyblades}}

ShelterDrake avatar.jpg ==Videos== 【ベイブレード開発者レビュー】ランダムブースター シェルタードレイクセレクト|Takara Tomy product overview BEYBLADE X - Unleashing SHELTER DRAKE 7-80GP- The Ultimate Defense & Stamina Bey from the BX Line!|Hasbro product overview ==Trivia== *ShelterDrake is the only Balance Type in the ''Drake'' series. *ShelterDrake is the first Beyblade that references a motif from a past generation to change its type. **In this case, ShelterDrake is a Balance type while [[Dragoon]] is an Attack type. *While the anime and manga describes ShelterDrake as having strong Attack and Defense capabilities, the Bey is promoted in the toyline as having high Defense and Stamina instead. **ShelterDrake's 4X avatar is a combination of ImpactDrake and BlackShell as an analogy of having both Attack and Defense capabilities. *Similar to BlackShell, ShelterDrake's 4X Avatar also spins itself like a drill as a Special Move. *This is the first Beyblade with the ''Drake'' motif not to be owned by [[Khrome Ryugu]]. *In the manga, Shelter Drake's Gear Point Bit is mistakenly illustrated as the [[Bit - }}{{Translation|'''Trypio 3-60N'''|トライピオ3-60N|Toraipio 3-60N|Trypio Three Sixty Needle}} is a Defense Type Beyblade and the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' remake of the [[Spin Gear System]] Beyblade [[Trypio]].

In an August 2023 poll conducted by [[Takara Tomy]] for the [[X-Over Project]], Trypio was voted as the #1 finalist. Two prototypes were developed, with the first one being unveiled at the ''X-Treme Cup'' G1 2023 event on December 9th, 2023.<ref>https://twitter.com/tbh_pr/status/1734043627796811908</ref>

However, on January 29th, 2024 the development team announced that Trypio remake had been canceled due to various safety issues, along with concerns about the marketability of the product.<ref>https://www.beach.jp/circleboard/af10964/topictree/1100217168165</ref> A major concern was that a Blader's fingers could get entangled in the Trypio Blade during a [[Launch]], due to the wide diameter of Trypio's design. While a second prototype with a smaller diameter was considered, designers felt that this design deviated too much from the original look and feel of Trypio, so ultimately shelved the release entirely.

parts.title: Asia Championship 2024
parts.text:
{{Tournament Infobox |Name=Asia Championship 2024 |Image=Asia Championship 2024.png |ImageCaption=Official Logo |Series=Beyblade X |Host=[[Beyblade Battle Base]] (B4) |Location=Sunshine City
Tokyo, Japan |ParticipantCount=20 |Prize=[[DranBuster 1-60A]] Gold Plated Trophy |Champion=Zane (open class)
Sousuke (regular class) |RunnerUp=Mi Hee Youn (open class)
Emmanuel Marcelino (regular class) |Date=December 1st, 2024[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/g2_asia2024.html Official page (in Japanese)] |Start=10:30 AM |Finish=5:30 PM |Length=7 hours }}The {{Translation|'''Asia Championship 2024'''|アジアチャンピオンシップ 2024|Ajia Chanpionshippu 2024}} was an international Beyblade championship held on December 1st, 2024 at Sunshine City in Tokyo, Japan. Representatives from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, and Indonesia competed. The representatives were winners of qualifying regular class competitions (elementary school students only) or open class competitions (elementary school students to adults).[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/g2_asia2024.html Official page (in Japanese)] ==Representatives== *Japan: Tatsuki (open class) and Sousuke (regular class) *Korea: Mi Hee Youn (open class) and Min Seo Jo (regular class) *Taiwan: Jerry (open class) and Eric (regular class) *China: Shun Da Gu (open class) and Shao Wei Yang (regular class) *Hong Kong: Jimmy Lam (open class) and Jarvis Law (regular class) *Singapore: Zane (open class) and Javier (regular class) *Malaysia: Crimson (open class) and Alvis (regular class) *Philippines: Mark Jules Barrentes (open class) and Emmanuel Marcelino (regular class) *Thailand: Por (open class) and Zenshi (regular class) *Indonesia: Abe (open class) and Khaleed (regular class) ==Battle method== The matches played on December 1st, 2024 consisted of [[3on3 Battle]] matches to 4 points. The tournament was played with a single-elimination bracket. ==Controversy== During the open class semi-final match between Zane (Singapore) and Por (Thailand), the judge incorrectly declared Zane the winner of the fourth and final battle, despite Zane's WizardRod 9-60FB Bursting first. The score at the time was Zane with 3 points, and Por with 0 points. Zane's Free Ball (FB) Bit separated and went into the Xtreme Zone from the first hit, with Por's AeroPegasus Blade separating from its 1-60 Ratchet and Rush (R) Bit afterwards on the second hit. A 2 point Burst Finish was immediately given to Zane, and Zane was declared the winner of the match, with a score of 4-0 (the maximum points in a match is 4). A possible explanation was the judge did not see Zane's Free Ball Bit separate and enter the Xtreme Zone due to their viewing angle. While online viewers commented on the situation on the livestream, no reversal was made, and the tournament proceeded with Por eliminated. Zane would go on to win the tournament. The YouTube livestream was later temporarily privated for edits to remove downtime between matches. The entirety of the match remains in the VOD. When the VOD was made public again, the comments section was disabled, likely due to the influx of comments regarding this incident. ==Trivia== ==External links== *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/g2_asia2024.html Official page (in Japanese)] *[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ceYk8x9L3UU Livestream on YouTube] ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Tournaments]] [[Category:Official Tournaments]] [[Category:International Tournaments]]

parts.title: Assist Blade - Heavy
parts.text:
{{Part Infobox |Image=AssistBladeHeavy.png |Name=Heavy |JPName=ヘビー |RomajiName=Hebī |ProductCode=CX-11 (Takara Tomy)
G3028 (Hasbro) |Classification=Assist Blade |Type=Balance |SpinDirection=Right-Spin |Weight=7.8 grams |System=Custom Line |Series=Beyblade X (Season 3) |ReleaseJP=November 1st, 2025 |ReleaseCA=June 20th, 2026 |ReleaseEU=March 1st, 2026 |AttackStat=17 |DefenseStat=17 |StaminaStat=11 |HeightStat=50 |XStandard=✔️ }}{{Translation|'''Heavy'''|ヘビー|Hebī}} is a [[Assist Blade]] released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the [[Custom Line]] system. It debuted in Japan with the release of the CX-11 [[EmperorMight Deck Set]] on November 1st, 2025. It later debuted in western countries with the release of [[Hasbro]]'s [[X-treme Battlers Pack]]. ==Description== '''Heavy''' is a low 50-height Assist Blade, with an aggressive six-bladed design. It is intended as an upgrade for [[DranBrave S6-60V]], replacing the Slash Assist Blade. At the time of writing, '''Heavy''' is the heaviest Assist Blade available, at an average weight of 7.8 grams. The design is best suited for Attack Type Main Blades, such as [[Main Blade - Brave|Brave (Courage)]] and [[Main Blade - Blast|Blast]], as the weight distribution amplifies the contact points, and unlike Assist Blades such as Wheel, '''Heavy''' allows the contact points to remain exposed. A special feature of '''Heavy''' is the addition of metal to increase centrifugal force and balance. Prior to the release of '''Heavy''', the heaviest Assist Blade was Wheel, which had an average weight of 7.2 grams. While Wheel was popular due to its heavy weight, its high 80-height round design meant Attack Type Main Blades had reduced Attack potential, but higher lategame Life-After-Death (LAD) rolling. As such, while Wheel is still favorable for Defense and Stamina builds, '''Heavy''' is an excellent choice for low-height Attack combinations. Compared to the initial CG renders, the actual product has two additional small blocky protrusions, creating a Burst risk. ==Overall== ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== * CX-11 [[EmperorMight Deck Set]] - [[EmperorMight HOp]] ===Hasbro=== * G3028 [[X-treme Battlers Pack]] - [[Might Emperor H Op]] ==Gallery== AssistBladeHeavy.png|Heavy (CX-11/G3028) ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Custom Line Parts}} [[Category:Takara Tomy]] [[Category:Hasbro]]

parts.title: Basic Line
parts.text:
[[File:Basic Line Logo.png|thumb|200px]]
[[File:Basic Line Expand Blade Logo.png|thumb|200px|Basic Line Expand Blade (Takara Tomy Logo)]]
[[File:Basic Line Version 2.0 Logo.png|thumb|200px|Basic Line Version 2.0]]

The {{Translation|'''Basic Line'''|ベーシックライン|Bēshikku Rain}} is the first Beyblade system of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. This line features a blue band on the packaging for its products.

For a list of parts in the '''Basic Line''' system, see [[List of Basic Line parts]].

==Structure==
{{QuotePart
|quote = Reliable performance, well-balanced and easy to control, ideal for beginners!
|speaker = Official Hasbro Description}}
A Basic Line Beyblade consists of three main components: the Blade, the Ratchet, and the Bit.

===Blade===
[[File:BladeDranSword.png|thumb|140px|DranSword Blade]]
[[File:BladeDranStrike.png|thumb|140px|DranStrike Blade]]

'''Blades''' are the top component of the Bey, and act as the main contact points. The center features a "Gear Chip" beneath transparent PMMA plastic, showcasing a paper cutout of the Bey's Avatar, with a symbol indicating the spin direction. The "Gear Chip" also rotates when connected to a Bit.  The contact points are made from zinc alloy, while the lower sections are made of PMMA.

Blades require three Launcher hooks for insertion, enabling the Bey to launch in either of the two required spin directions, whether clockwise or counterclockwise, depending on the Bey. Stoppers prevent the Bey from being spun in the wrong spin direction.

There are also Hasbro Debut Blades that use the same plastic components, but with differently designed metal components. 

In February 2026, the '''Expand Blade''' was introduced to extend the characteristics of the BX Line, making them more stable by connecting the metal in the center and increasing its rigidity. In addition, the paper cutout of the Bey's Avatar on the "Gear Chip" is replaced with a sticker, as well as the rotating "Gear Chip" removed for more rigidity in the Blade. 

In July 2026, the '''Version 2.0 Blade''' was introduced to the BX Line, where the blade is heavier and provides superior performances in battle. In addition, the paper cutout of the Bey's Avatar on the "Gear Chip" is given a holographic effect. 

===Ratchet===
[[File:Ratchet3-60.png|thumb|140px|3-60 Ratchet]]
'''Ratchets''' are the middle components of the Bey, attaching beneath the Blade.

They vary in height and contact point design. A Ratchet attaches to the Blade by twisting, which determines the amount of Burst Resistance in each Bey. Spin direction can be changed by manually twisting the outer portion of the Ratchet, indicated by "'''L'''" or "'''R'''" spots on the Ratchet as a guide for proper assembly. 

'''Simple Type Ratchets''' (Hasbro: "RBT-Ratchet") use "O-type joint", that snaps onto the Blade, rather than the standard Ratchet joints that rotate to click into place. 

===Bit===
[[File:BitFlat.png|thumb|60px|Flat Bit]]
'''Bits''' act as the main contact points with the stadium floor. Most Bits have the standard 12 tooth gear that interact with the gears on the "X-Celerator Rail" ("Xtreme Line") of the [[Xtreme Stadium]], increasing the Bey's speed. Some Bits have alternate number of tooth gears that changes the speed and frequencies of Xtreme Dashes.

These are the additional subtype series of Bits aside from the standard:
*'''Low Bits,''' which are 1mm shorter
*'''High Bits,''' which are 1mm taller
*'''Gear Bits,''' which have extended teeth to catch onto the X-Celerator Rail easier
*'''Disk Bits,''' which have a outer disk that enhance its ability to produce and maintain centrifugal force
*'''Metal Bits,''' which have metal contact points
*'''Free Bits,''' which spins freely from the Ratchet
*'''Trans Bits,''' which changes the height of the Bey when performing an Xtreme Dash
*'''Bound Bits,''' which produces shock absorptions with the floor of the Xtreme Stadium
*'''Rubber Bits,''' which have rubber contact points
*'''Under Bits,''' which are 2mm shorter
*'''Wall Bits,''' which have a bumpy ring that makes contact with the floor of the Xtreme Stadium to aid the Bey in staying upright
*'''Ratchet-integrated Bit''' (Hasbro: "Combo Ratchet-Bit"), which integrates the Ratchet and Bit together

==Gallery==

Basic Line Promo.png
Basic Line Expand Blade Promo.png
</gallery>

==Trivia==
* Basic Line Blades generally use the same Launcher hook designs for similar motifs or for the same team in the ''[[Beyblade X (Season 1)|Beyblade X]]'' anime and manga.
** For example, [[Blade - DranSword|DranSword]], [[HellsScythe 4-60T|HellsScythe]] and [[Blade - WizardArrow|WizardArrow]] share the same same Launcher hook design as they belong to [[Persona]].
** [[Blade - CobaltDragoon|CobaltDragoon]], [[Blade - WeissTiger|WeissTiger]], [[Blade - BlackShell|BlackShell]] and [[Blade - CrimsonGaruda|CrimsonGaruda]] share the same same Launcher hook design as their motifs are the Four Auspicious Beasts from Chinese mythology.
** [[Blade - CobaltDrake|CobaltDrake]], [[Blade - TriceraPress|TriceraPress]], [[Blade - SamuraiCalibur|SamuraiCalibur]] and the Collaboration Blades appear to be the exceptions to this rule.

==Appearance==

==Biography==
The King of Bey Kingdom has recently collapsed but is currently in stable condition. He made a suprising decision to name the next monarch while he is still alive.

The King has 99 children and he will use Beyblading to determine his next successor through the Spin Crown Wars. The last one standing will become the ruler of Bey Kingdom.

It is also suspected that some of the princes might be planning something sinister, like selling off their positions or statuses to people from other countries in order to gain the monarchy if they win.

|Series=Beyblade Burst
|Series2=Beyblade X
}}'''Bey Points''' are awarded by [[Takara Tomy]] to Bladers who participate in official tournaments, buy products, and use the companion product with the app.

== How to obtain Bey Points. ==
There are several ways to obtain Bey Points.
* If you win wbba. tournaments, Bey Points will be awarded. (For G4 tournaments, points will be awarded with Bey Code Cards)
* By scanning the Bey Code Cards that come with your Beyblade purchases, you can redeem Bey Points.
* You can get Bey Points by going through special training with your Beylogger or Beylogger Plus.
* If you make two Beyloggers friends, both Beyloggers respective accounts will receive a number of Bey Points.

== What can you do with Bey Points? ==
You can accumulate your Bey Points and then do the [[Rare Bey Get Battle (Burst)|Rare Bey Get Battle]] challenge. If you win the challenge, you get a prize.

}}The {{Translation|'''Beybattle Pass'''|ベイバトルパス|Beibatoru Pasu}}, stylized '''BEYBATTLEPASS''', is an Accessory released as part of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. It was released in Japan on July 15th, 2023 for 3300円.

==Description==
The '''Beybattle Pass''' is primarily used to interact with [[Takara Tomy]]'s [[Beyblade X (app)|''Beyblade X'' mobile app]] via Bluetooth, allowing a Blader to participate in-app to earn Beypoints for the "Rare Bey Get Battle" gacha lottery. It also measures Shoot Power (launch strength), and using the '''Beybattle Pass''' offline will record launches, which can then be used to earn more Beypoints. It attaches to the top of a launcher, using a protrusion in the center to record Shoot Power. With batteries inside, the '''Beybattle Pass''' also adds weight, and can be used to make a launcher easier to hold onto. It is not compatible with the [[Entry Launcher (Beyblade X)|Entry Launcher]] or [[Clip & Rip Launcher]].

Like all ''Beyblade X'' products, the '''Beybattle Pass''' includes a Bey Code on the right-side box flap. When this Bey Code is scanned, the Blader will receive 3300 Beypoints, and scanning additional product Bey Codes afterwards will earn them a bonus 100 Bey Points. All product Bey Codes are one-time use only, and registering the '''Beybattle Pass''' itself will not grant the aforementioned bonus. In other words, second-hand used '''Beybattle Pass''' do not grant an account this bonus.

Bī Fō |AKA=B4 |Status=Active |Country=Worldwide |Series=Beyblade X }}The {{Translation|'''Beyblade Battle Base'''|ベイブレード バトル ベース|Beiburēdo Batoru Bēsu}}, also known by the abbreviation {{Ruby|'''B4'''|ビーフォー}}, is an organization in ''[[Beyblade X]]''. B4 is the ''[[Beyblade X (generation)|Beyblade X]]'' successor to the previous [[wbba.]], [[WBBA]], and [[BBA]] organizations. Official [[Takara Tomy]] "Gear Sports" tournaments, including those held in sponsored stores, are held under the B4 banner. B4 is also responsible for the organization of major international tournaments. ==Fictional== In the anime and manga, B4 serves as the world Beyblade management organization, and manages the [[X Tower]]. The ''Pro League'' is a sports league and the top level of professional Beyblading in the world. ==Structure== Similar to previous series, there are different grades of competition. Prizes will differ depending on the tournament grade. Only elementary school students are eligible for "''Regular''"-class tournaments. "''Open''"-class tournaments are open to Bladers of all ages. *'''[[Beyblade X Grand Prix Final 2026]]''' - International Beyblade championship. *'''[[Beyblade X World Championship 2025|World Championship]]''' - International Beyblade championship. *'''[[Asia Championship 2024|Asia Championship]]''' - International Beyblade championship with representatives from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, and Indonesia. *'''GP (Grand Prix)''' - The pinnacle national tournament where the top Bladers are decided. The representatives for the "''Regular''" and "''Open''" tournaments of the international Grand Prix Final/World Championship/Asia Championship tournaments are decided here. *'''G1 (Grade 1)''' - Tournaments held by B4 at large venues. *'''G2 (Grade 2)''' - Tournaments held by B4 at large venues or at B4 sponsored stores. *'''G3 (Grade 3)''' - Monthly tournaments held at B4 sponsored stores. *'''S1 (Street 1)''' - Events that can be held by Bladers themselves. A form must be filled out and submitted through an official B4 sponsored store. ==History== The first G2 tournament, the "X-Treme Cup", was held between August and October 2023 in 4 different cities. Participation was open to elementary school students and older. The entry fee was 6,000 yen (tax included) and included a tournament uniform, which must be worn during the tournament. The first G1 tournament, the "X-Treme Cup", was a ''Regular''-class tournament held on December 9 and 10, 2023. Participation was limited to elementary school students and older. The entry fee was 3,000 yen (tax included) and includes a "G1 Special Battle Pass Sheet" for the [[Beybattle Pass]], and 1000 Beypoints. Participation was limited to a lottery, where 512 winners could play. The top 16 players of the first day's qualifying tournament then proceeded to the second day's finals tournament. The first GP tournament, the "[[X-Treme Cup GP 2024]]" was held in the second half of 2024. Several qualifying tournaments were held throughout Japan in the months of August and September, with a final tournament at [[wikipedia:Sunshine City, Tokyo|Sunshine City]] in Tokyo on October 27th, 2024. The "X-Treme Cup GP 2024" consisted of ''Open''-class tournaments, meaning Bladers of any age could participate. The ''Regular''-class equivalent was the "[[Japan Championship 2024]]", which was restricted to elementary school students. The winners of the "X-Treme Cup GP 2024" and "Japan Championship 2024" were "Tatsuki" of [[WARIBEY]] and "13-Sousuke" respectively. These two Bladers would later represent Japan at the "Asia Championship 2024" tournament. ==Tournament List== For the sake of brevity, only international and Japanese tournaments are listed. G3 tournaments and S1 events are not listed. ===International Tournaments=== *''[[Asia Championship 2024]]'' (December 2024) ===Grand Prix Tournaments=== *''[[X-Treme Cup GP 2024]]'' (''Open'' Class) **Preliminary rounds (August and September 2024) **Final tournament (October 27th, 2024) *''[[Japan Championship 2024]]'' (''Regular'' Class) **Preliminary rounds (August and September 2024) **Final tournament (October 27th, 2024) ===Grade 1 Tournaments=== *''X-Treme Cup'' (December 9 and 10, 2023) ===Grade 2 Tournaments=== *''X-Treme Cup'' (August and October 2023) *''Katsushika Cup'' (April 6, 2024) ==Trivia== *The organization's abbreviation, "B4", refers to the four "B"s in its full name. *The page URLs for the [[Asia Championship 2024]] and [[Japan Championship 2024]] refer to the tournaments as G2 and G1 respectively, although they do not follow typical tournament structures. ==External links== *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/ Official webpage on Takara Tomy's website] *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/g1.html Official webpage on G1 tournaments] *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/g2.html Official webpage on G2 tournaments] *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/b4.html Official webpage on G3 tournaments] *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/beyblade-x/event/s1.html Official webpage on S1 events] ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Beyblade X]]

}}The '''Beyblade X''' series consists of the ''[[Beyblade X (Season 1)|Beyblade X]]'' anime, which is adapted from the ''[[List of Beyblade X chapters|Beyblade X]]'' manga. It is also referred to as '''Generation 4''' by [[Hasbro]].

==Information==
'''Beyblade X''' is a Japanese manga and toyline created as part of [[Takara Tomy]]'s ''[[Beyblade (franchise)|Beyblade]]'' franchise. The fourth incarnation of the franchise after the [[Burst Series]], the ''Beyblade X'' toyline was launched on June 10th, 2023 at the CoroCoro Spirit Festival, accompanied by a manga series in June 2023 and later an anime adaptation in October 2023.

parts.text:
{{Chapter Infobox |DubTitle = X |Image = X01.webp |JPTitle = {{Ruby|X|エックス}} |RomajiTitle = Ekkusu |TransTitle = X |Series = Beyblade X |Magazine = CoroCoro Comic |Volume = 1 |Chapter = 1 |Pages = 70 |ReleaseJP = June 15th, 2023 |ReleaseEN = |PrevChap = [[Beyblade X - Special Chapter 01]] |NextChap = [[Beyblade X - Chapter 02|Rainbow]] |Anime=[[Beyblade X - Episode 01|01]] (p.1-62)
[[Beyblade X - Episode 02|02]] (p.62-69) }}{{Translation|"'''X'''"|{{Ruby|X|エックス}}|Ekkusu|X}} is the first chapter of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' manga. It was first released in the July issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on June 15th, 2023 and was later released in Volume 1 of the Tankobon on September 28th, 2023. ==Plot== We cut to battle against Team Pendragon and an unknown team and Team Pendragon wins being crowned "Champions of the X". We then cut to Robin and his friends and Robin is excited to be in Xenon City and is ready to become a Pro Blader and reaching the top of the X. Robin's team makes it to Ameteur matches and Robin is beaten by Team Phalanx lead by Takumi Ishiyama. Takumi wins against Robin and shatters his Beyblade Strike Hawk right in front of his eyes. After the battle, Robin learns that his friends want to disband the team and he is left all alone. Soon after an unknown masked blader speaks out to him. One look of his mask and Robin is terrified, the blader then tells Robin he saw his teammates ditch him and then tells him that battles are usually done in teams of 3 and figured he wanted help refilling his team. Robin then notices the blader's beyblade as Sword Dran and believes it's a fake but putting that aside the blader reminds him that if he stays a lone wolf the path to becoming a Pro will be even more tough and then Robin decides to let the blader in and they create Team Persona. The two then arrive at another Amateur match where Robin asks for the blader's name and the blader says for Robin to call him Blader X. Blader X is ready to battle but Robin stops him as he states he doesn't have a beyblade anymore thanks to Takumi who they notice to shatter another Beyblade. Even with Robin's warning, Blader X challenges Team Phalanx with Multi noticing. Robin tells Blader X that he shouldn't battle them since they're pros. Takumi tells Robin he is a weakling and he has no right to blade but Blader X helps him by saying if he is weak or no good as long as he has fun he wins. Takumi doubts it but Blader X says if he says weak bladers shouldn't be blading he would have to quit, and in the end Blader X and Team Phalanx battle. Before the first battle, Blader X tells Robin what the X meant in his name and in the first battle with Genri, he won so fast nobody's eyes could see it and then in the second battle against Takumi he won with an extreme dash and Robin remebered the importance of having fun with beyblading. Blader X and Robin then go out for some sushi and then Robin then tells Blader X he knew who he was. He thought he was Chrome Ryugu but he was wrong and Blader X is really former member of Team Pendragon, Jaxon Cross! Jaxon also explains that Sword Dran is actually his beyblade but only lent it to Chrome. Robin then asks why Jaxon a champion is with ameteurs and says he thought it could be fun and asks if it's enough. Though he eventually tells Robin why he really quit Pendragon. He told him that was at the top he realized that he couldn't battle anyone that could give him a real challenge but then saw that there was. Jaxon quit because he's climbing his way back up to the top of the X to challenge Chrome. Robin thinks he is unbelieveable and then thinks he could become much stronger. ==Major Events== * Jaxon, and his Sword Dran, Robin Kazami, Khrome Ryugu, Multi Nana-iro, and Takumi Ishiyama make their debuts. * Khrome and his team, [[Pendragon]], are crowned the champions of [[The X]]. * Robin and his team, Albatross Strikers, arrive in X City. * Robin and Takumi face off, with the latter winning and destroying the former's Bey. * Following Robin's defeat to Takumi, Albatross Strikers is disbanded. Robin is then encountered by Blader X, who asks if he'd like to join his team, [[Persona]], in which he accepts. * Robin and Blader X arrive at the Amateur Arena where the latter takes on Genri and Takumi and defeats them both. * After watching Blader X's battles, Robin's motivation returns. * Blader X reveals his true identity to be Jaxon Cross, a former member of Pendragon. * Jaxon reveals that he left Pendragon and became Blader X so he could reclimb [[The X]] with his own team to battle [[Khrome Ryugu]]. ==Characters== *[[Robin Kazami]] *[[Khrome Ryugu]] *[[Jaxon Cross]] *[[Sigrid Nana-iro]] *[[Takumi Ishiyama]] (Debut) *[[Genri Sayo]] (Debut) *[[Bariki Jinnai]] (Debut) ==Beyblades== *[[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]] (Jaxon's; Used by Khrome) *[[Strike Hawk]] (Robin's; Destroyed) *[[Stone Mont Blanc|Stone Mountain]] (Takumi's; Debut) *[[Iron Forest]] (Genri's; Debut) *[[Diamond Nut]] (Bariki's; Debut) ==Featured Battles== {{Battle |name = Khrome Ryugu vs. Unknown Blader |team1players = [[Khrome Ryugu]] |team2players = Unknown Blader |team1beys = [[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]] |team2beys = Unknown Bey |team1result = Win |team2result = Lose |notes = * Round 1: Khrome & Sword Dran (Xtreme Finish; 3pts)}} {{Battle |name = Takumi Ishiyama vs. Robin Kazami |team1players = [[Takumi Ishiyama]] |team2players = [[Robin Kazami]] |team1beys = [[Stone Mont Blanc|Stone Mountain]] |team2beys = [[Strike Hawk]] |team1result = Win |team2result = Lose |notes = * Round 1: Takumi & Stone Mountain}} {{Battle |name = Jaxon Cross (Blader X) vs. Genri Sayo |team1players = [[Jaxon Cross]] (Blader X) |team2players = [[Genri Sayo]] |team1beys = [[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]] |team2beys = [[Iron Forest]] |team1result = Win |team2result = Lose |notes = * Round 1: Blader X & Sword Dran}} {{Battle |name = Jaxon Cross (Blader X) vs. Takumi Ishiyama |team1players = [[Jaxon Cross]] (Blader X)

It was first released in the August issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on July 14th, 2023 and was later released in Volume 1 of the Tankobon on September 28th, 2023. ==Plot== A happy Jaxon then tells Robin it's a great day for Beyblading and lists the conditions that are great for blading. Soon fans notice him, they focus really on Jaxon more than Robin. After Jaxon tells Robin about a surprise Pro -Selection match that day. Robin then freaks out and yells at Jaxon why he didn't tell him and that he doesn't a beyblade anymore and then Jaxon starts to freak out. Multi then walks in and offers Robin a new Beyblade from her collection and his eye catches Scythe Incendio. Robin is given Scythe Incendio and the two go to the match. At the Pro-Selection match Jaxon and Robin realize that they are battling the person who gave Robin his new partner who's name is Multi Nana-iro is flying solo. Robin has no idea who she is but her fans tell her. At the battle Robin battles using Jaxon's blading style and thinks he will win but little did he know he was playing into her hand. After Blader X tells Robin that he will take care of it, Robin thinks he will win for sure but Multi has a back-up plan and changes both her outfit and beyblade. At the match Jaxon talks about how the match will be done fast, the two launch at the battle Multi launches at a tilted angle to maximize Helm Knight's Defence, but then Jaxon comes in with an Extreme Dash but Multi doesn't lose yet and thinks she wins but Jaxon the "X-traordinary" part starts now as he pulls off a second X-treme dash and knocks out Helm Knight, wins the battle, and he and Robin are now seen as Pro Bladers. Multi couldn't believe she lost and even starts crying, Jaxon then walks over to her, reveals his identity from his Blader X helmet and asks her if she wants to join their team. Multi accepts. ==Major Events== * Multi Nana-iro and her Arrow Wizard and Helm Knight and Robin's Scythe Incendio make their debuts. * Jaxon and Robin are encountered by Multi Nana-iro, who offers to give Robin a new Bey to replace his shattered Strike Hawk, which he is given Scythe Incendio. * In the Professional Selection Match, Team Persona faces off with Team Rainbow, with Multi being the only member of the latter team. * Robin and Multi face off, with the latter winning and taking the first point for her team. * Jaxon and Multi face off, with the former winning two points and winning the match. * Multi disbands her team in order to join [[Persona|Team Persona]]. ==Characters== *[[Jaxon Cross]] *[[Robin Kazami]] *[[Takumi Ishiyama]] (Flashback) *[[Multi Nana-iro]] (Debut) ==Beyblades== *[[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]] (Jaxon's) *[[Strike Hawk]] (Robin's; Debut) ==Featured Battles== {{Battle |name = Multi Nana-iro vs. Bird Kazami |team1players = [[Multi Nana-iro]] |team2players = [[Robin Kazami]] |team1beys = [[WizardArrow 4-80B|Arrow Wizard 4-80B]] |team2beys = [[HellsScythe 4-60T|Scythe Incendio 4-60T]] |team1result = Win |team2result = Lose |notes = * Round 1: Multi & Arrow Wizard (Ring-Out Finish)}} {{Battle |name = Multi Nana-iro vs. Jaxon Cross |team1players = [[Multi Nana-iro]] |team2players = [[Jaxon Cross]] |team1beys = [[KnightShield 3-80N|Helm Knight 3-80N]] |team2beys = [[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]] |team1result = Lose |team2result = Win |notes = * Round 1: Jaxon & Sword Dran (Ring-Out Finish)}} ==Special Moves Used== *[[Xtreme Dash]] ([[HellsScythe 4-60T|Scythe Incendio 4-60T]] (Mimicked and Mastered) & [[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]]) *[[Mirage Parry]] ([[WizardArrow 4-80B|Arrow Wizard 4-80B]]) *[[Xtreme Dash Double]] ([[DranSword 3-60F|Sword Dran 3-60F]]) ==Gallery== ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{X Chapters}}

}}{{Translation|"'''Bey Sponsor'''"|ベイスポンサー|Bei Suponsā|Bey Sponsor}} is the third chapter of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' manga. It was first released in the September issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on August 12th, 2023 and was later released in Volume 1 of the Tankobon on September 28th, 2023.

==Plot==
The chapter starts with Team Persona celebrates them reaching Pro Blader status. Though, Multi says that they are not technically pro bladers yet, and how they need one certain thing. When Robin asks what it is, Jaxon answers his question by saying that they need the one thing that every Pro Team must have, a Bey Sponsor. Multi explains that sponsors are companies that support bladers while the bladers support the sponsor’s business. Jaxon then says that he already found a sponsor that they will be meeting tomorrow. However, much to Multi and Robin’s disappointment it is a sushi restaurant called Komaba Sushi. Team Persona then meet Taisho Sushiya and Meiko Myoden, and the team is put to the test in a battle that determines if they get sponsored by Komaba Sushi or not. The challenge is to win against Meiko Myoden and Robin ends up losing in the first battle, but Multi was able to win which meant that Team Persona got their sponsor.

==Major Events==
* To officially obtain their Pro team status, [[Persona]] heads to [[Komaba Sushi]] in search of a sponsor.
* Meiko Myoden and her Keel Shark and Multi's Lance Knight make their debuts.
* Before making the sponsorship official, Meiko faces Robin and Multi to battle in which 1 of the 2 Bladers must win.
** In the first battle, Robin and Meiko face off with the latter winning.
** In the second battle, Multi and Meiko face off with the former winning.
* Due to Persona completing the challenge, the sponsorship becomes official and Persona becomes recognized as a Pro team.

{{Translation|"'''Zooganic'''"|ズーガニック|Zūganikku|Zooganic}} is the fourth chapter of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' manga. It was first released in the October issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on September 15th, 2023 and was later released in Volume 1 of the Tankobon on September 28th, 2023.

==Plot==

==Major Events==
* In a flashback, Jaxon's final match with Khrome before departing from [[Pendragon]] is revealed.
* Now that they've become Pro Bladers, Persona enters [[The X]].

==Plot==

==Major Events==
* The All-Star Battle is revealed.
** Team Persona took first place in the team votes. If they win, they will be able to challenge at the top of the X.
** For the individual votes, Packun took third place, Rex Jura took second place and Quinn Manju took first place, forming the temporary Team [[Dreams]].
* The All-Star Battle begins, which is set to have each Blader face off with each other in a single elimination format until the team with the last blader standing wins.

** It is also revealed that Khrome does not need Blader X anymore, stating that he has become one with Jaxon and has surpassed him.

It was first released in the September 2024 issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on August 9th, 2024 and was later released in Volume 4 of the Tankobon on October 28th, 2024.

==Plot==
==Major Events==
* It is revealed that the battle between Buster Dran and Cobalt Dragoon ends in the draw. However, Buster Dran has cracked in the process.
* It is revealed that Khrome performed an Xtreme Dash technique that uses the full rotation of the Xtreme Line, which is called "Dragonic Break".
* Khrome requested Jaxon to switch the damaged Buster Dran out for Dagger Dran.
** A flashback reveals that on the day Jaxon left, Jaxon thought Khrome was going easy on him, leading to Khrome resenting him.
* Jaxon and Khrome continue their face-off in the second round, with both Beys performing Xtreme Dash Infinite and ending in a second draw.
** It is revealed that Khrome is deliberately adapting Blader X's tactics to show the difference in their abilities.
** Dagger Dran has also cracked in the process.
** Khrome requested Jaxon to switch the damaged Dagger Dran out for Sword Dran.
* Jaxon and Khrome end their face-off in the third round, with the former winning by using Khrome's "Dragonic Break" technique against him. Khrome also subsequently fainted from the match.
* It is revealed that the identity of Blader Z is Ciel Kaminari, who now wishes to avenge Khrome by defeating Blader X.
* Robin and Ciel face off in the third match, with the later winning.
** Like Jaxon, Robin is able to use Khrome's "Dragonic Break" technique. However, his Hammer Incendio bursts right before it can end the match with an Xtreme Finish.
** Robin annouced that even though he won, he felt the battle was fun.
* Pendragon remains as the champion team on the X.

It was first released in the October issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on September 13th, 2024 and was later released in Volume 5 of the Tankobon on January 28th, 2025. ==Plot== ==Major Events== * Tenka arrives at Komaba Sushi to battle Blader X but is declined by Taisho. ** It is revealed Tenka is an instructor at the Shiroboshi School dojo. * Tenka's Saber Samurai and Meiko's Tide Whale make their debuts. * Tenka decides to challenge Persona and Meiko, claiming to defeat all of them. ** Tenka and Meiko face off in the first match, with the former winning. ** Tenka and Multi face off in the second match, with the former winning. * When Jaxon returns to Komaba Sushi as Blader X, Tenka challenges Jaxon, with them making a bet. ** If Tenka wins, Jaxon must obey all of her orders. ** If Tenka loses, she must give him what he wants. ** Tenka and Jaxon face off, with the latter winning. ** It is revealed that Tenka wants to bring Jaxon to fight against the strongest Blader, making the outcomes of the bet having no difference. ** Jaxon accepts Tenka's offer. ==Characters== *[[Number One]] *[[Titus Manju]] *[[Blaze Fujiwara]] *[[Sigrid Nana-iro]] *[[Khrome Ryugu]] *[[Ciel Kaminari]] *[[Jian Strong]] *[[Toguro Okunaga]] *[[Yuni Naniwa]] *[[Zonamos Nekoyama]] *[[Robin Kazami]] *[[Multi Nana-iro]] *[[Taisho Sushiya]] *[[Jaxon Cross]] *[[Tenka Shiroboshi]] (debut) *[[Meiko Myoden]] ==Beyblades== *[[PhoenixRudder 9-70G|Rudder Phoenix 9-70G]] (Blaze's; It was first released in the November issue of [[CoroCoro Comic]] on October 15th, 2024 and was later released in Volume 5 of the Tankobon on January 28th, 2025. ==Plot== ==Major Events== *Jaxon allows Tenka to bring him to fight against the strongest Blader on one condition - he must form a team with her. ** It is revealed that Jaxon's master, Ginro has also asked him to join their team. * Ginro and his Sterling Wolf, along with the [[Wide Xtreme Stadium]] make their debuts. * Two Pros challenge Ginro with fake replicas of both of Khrome's Cobalt Drake and Cobalt Dragoon but are defeated. * Jaxon's identity is accidentally revealed to Tenka by Ginro. ** It is revealed that Ginro wants to form a team with Jaxon to fight against an organization of underground Pros who are reaching for world domination. * Tenka challenges Ginro, with the winner being able to get Jaxon on their team. ** Jaxon, Tenka and Ginro face off with Jaxon winning. ** Jaxon offers Tenka to join Persona. ==Characters== *[[Tenka Shiroboshi]] *[[Jaxon Cross]] *[[Multi Nana-iro]] *[[Robin Kazami]] *[[Taisho Sushiya]] *[[Meiko Myoden]] *[[Ginro]] (debut) ==Beyblades== *[[CobaltDrake 4-60F|Cobalt Drake 4-60F]] (replica) *[[CobaltDragoon 2-60C|Cobalt Dragoon 2-60C]] (replica) *[[SilverWolf 3-80FB|Sterling Wolf 3-80FB]] (Ginro's; debut) *[[SamuraiSaber 2-70L|Saber Samurai 2-70L]] (Tenka's) *[[DranBuster 1-60A|Buster Dran 1-60A]] (Jaxon's) ==Featured Battles== {{Battle |name = Ginro vs. Shadow Pros - Wide Xtreme Stadium |team1players = [[Ginro]] |team2players = Two Shadow Pros |team1beys = [[SilverWolf 3-80FB|Sterling Wolf 3-80FB]] |team2beys = [[CobaltDrake 4-60F|Cobalt Drake 4-60F]]
[[CobaltDragoon 2-60C|Cobalt Dragon 2-60C]] |team1result = Win |team2result = Lose |notes = *Round 1: Ginro & Sterling Wolf - Double Knockout Finish; 4pts }} {{BattleFFA |name = Ginro vs. Tenka vs Jaxon - Wide Xtreme Stadium |player1 = [[Ginro]] |player2 = [[Tenka Shiroboshi]] |player3 = [[Jaxon Cross]] |player1bey = [[SilverWolf 3-80FB|Sterling Wolf 3-80FB]] |player2bey = [[SamuraiSaber 2-70L|Saber Samurai 2-70L]] |player3bey = [[DranBuster 1-60A|Buster Dran 1-60A]] |result=Win |winner= Jaxon Cross |notes = *Round 1: Jaxon & Buster Dran - Double Knockout Finish; 4pts }} ==Special Moves Used== *[[Xtreme Dash Double Cross]] ([[CobaltDrake 4-60F|Cobalt Drake 4-60F]] & [[CobaltDragoon 2-60C|Cobalt Dragoon 2-60C]]) *[[Hyper Boost Volgdrive]] ([[SilverWolf 3-80FB|Sterling Wolf 3-80FB]]) *[[Glimmering Stars]] ([[SamuraiSaber 2-70L|Saber Samurai 2-70L]]) *[[Xtreme Dash Buster]] ([[DranBuster 1-60A|Buster Dran 1-60A]]) ==Gallery== ==Trivia== * Robin makes a reference to the [[CoroCoro Comic|CoroCoro comics]], the magazine in which the Beyblade X manga is published in, when Ginro is talking about the Shadow Pros. ** It is possible that the Underground Pros is also a reference to the trope of evil organisations in [[Hades Inc.|previous]] ''[[Dark Nebula|Beyblade]]'' [[Snake Pit Organization|series]], as fans have joked about the absurdity of these evil organisations wanting world domination through Beyblades. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{X Chapters}}

==Major Events==
* Six Cross and his Whip Brachio make their debuts.
* On the 60th floor of [[The True X]], Zero begins to trial [[Persona]] to see who will battle in the New Xtreme Battle, starting off with Robin and putting him against Six as well as making him use a replica of Whip Brachio to try and get him out.
* It is revealed that Six used to be the weakest Blader of the Cross family, but after being given a prototype of Whip Brachio and being told to just improve his launch, he later becomes one of the strongest Bladers in the family, even surpassing One in launch strength.
* After battling for over three hours, Robin's launch gradually improves after copying Six's launch form, causing the latter to get frustrated and forfeit the challenge, leading to Robin passing the test.

==Plot==

==Major Events==
* Following the True Xtreme Battle, Zero confirms to [[Persona]] that Jaxon is not actually his son and informs Jaxon that he may be able to find an answer in the [[Bey Kingdom]] where the team then sets out for.
* On the way to the Bey Kingdom, Persona is approached by Dima Dil Kanz, the 88th prince of the Kingdom, who gives Jaxon and Multi "V2 Blade" versions of their Sword Dran, Arrow Wizard, and Helm Knight.
** Except for Robin's Scythe Incendio as the Incendio series is still in developement, since Robin's true capabilities are unknown.
* Persona and Dima are approached by the Bey Kingdom's Anti-Royalist Faction, who challenges them in attempt to take Dima.
** Robin faces off with them in the first battle, but is defeated.
** Jaxon faces off with them in the second battle and wins.
* After realizing that Jaxon was noted as a member of Persona by the Anti-Royalist Faction, Robin and Multi realize that this was a fake kidnapping and the leader of the group reveals herself as Kiwami Miyazukae, who was actually hired by Dima to be his private secretary.
* It is revealed that the king of the Bey Kingdom had collapsed and decided to name the next monarch while he was still alive with the Spin Crown Wars, to which Dima asks for Persona's help since he had been declared to not battle again after an injury on his right-arm which Persona accepts.

Runner-up: [[Strike Dran 4-50FF]] (Metal Coat: Silver) |Champion=[https://worldbeyblade.org/User-Hottest1022 Newton] |RunnerUp=TBA |Date=August 29th, 2026[https://beyblade.com/gpfinal2026/#national Grand Prix Final 2026 official page] |Start=TBA |Finish=TBA |Length=TBA }}The '''Beyblade X Grand Prix 2026''' is a pair of upcoming Canadian regular-class and open-class tournaments held on August 29th, 2026. The venue is the [[wikipedia:West Edmonton Mall|West Edmonton Mall]] shopping mall, in Edmonton, Alberta. The winners of the 2 regional tournaments, 1 previously held in Toronto the month prior, and 1 held on the same day in Edmonton, participated in this national tournament. ==Attendees== Regular-class and open-class tournaments were held in Vaughan and Edmonton, on July 25th and August 29th, respectively. The 2 winners from these regional tournaments then competed against each other on August 29th, after the Edmonton qualifier tournament was completed. ===Vaughan=== The first qualifier tournament was held on July 25th at [[wikipedia:Vaughan Mills|Vaughan Mills]] shopping mall, in Vaughan, Ontario. The regular-class tournament was held in the morning and the open-class tournament was held in the afternoon. The participant count was capped at 128, with a lottery being held on-site to determine who would play. The lottery itself was capped at 500. Regular-class registration ran from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM, and 30 Bladers ultimately participated in the regular-class tournament that took place from 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM, which ended 2 hours ahead of schedule. Open-class registration still ran during the scheduled 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM, with 128 participants selected randomly to play. As there were 154 applicants, 26 Bladers did not play. ===Edmonton=== The second qualifier tournament was held the same day and venue as the national tournament. ===Winning Combos=== ==Available Equipment== The equipment and rules of the national tournament were the same as the previously held regional tournaments. All matches were played in [[Hasbro]]'s [[Xtreme Beystadium]]. A legal products list was provided, which included some, but not all, of the Hasbro products available in Canada at the time. Parts that were released after the Vaughan qualifier and allowed at the Edmonton qualifier are indicated with strikethrough text. The following parts were not allowed: ===Blade=== *[[Blade - AeroPegasus|Aero Pegasus]] *[[Blade - Rock Leone|Rock Leone]] *[[Blade - Lightning L-Drago (Rapid-Hit Type)|Lightning L-Drago (Rapid-Hit Type)]] *[[Blade - Lightning L-Drago (Upper Type)|Lightning L-Drago (Upper Type)]] *[[Blade - XenoXcalibur|Xeno Xcalius]] ===Lock Chip=== *[[Lock Chip - Brachio|Brachio]] *[[Lock Chip - Drake|Drake]] *[[Lock Chip - Phoenix|Phoenix]] *[[Lock Chip - Sol|Sol]] *[[Lock Chip - Unicorn|Unicorn]] *[[Lock Chip - Valkyrie|Valkyrie]] *[[Lock Chip - Wolf|Wolf]] ===Main Blade=== *[[Main Blade - Eclipse|Eclipse]] *[[Main Blade - Hunt|Hunt]] *[[Main Blade - Flare|Radiance]] *[[Main Blade - Volt|Volt]] ===Over Blade=== *[[Over Blade - Outer|Outer]] *[[Over Blade - Peak|Peak]] ===Metal Blade=== *[[Metal Blade - Delta|Delta]] *[[Metal Blade - Whip|Whip]] ===Assist Blade=== *[[Assist Blade - Dual|Dual]] *[[Assist Blade - Free|Free]] *[[Assist Blade - Gravity|Gravity]] *[[Assist Blade - Massive|Massive]] *[[Assist Blade - Odd|Odd]] *[[Assist Blade - Zillion|Zillion]] ===Ratchet=== *[[Ratchet - 0-60|0-60]] *[[Ratchet - 1-70|1-70]] *[[Ratchet - 2-80|2-80]] ===Bit=== *[[Bit - Gear Unite|Gear Unite (GU)]] *[[Bit - Narrow|Narrow (Nr)]] *[[Bit - Trans Kick|Trans Kick (TK)]] *[[Bit - Wall Wedge|Wall Wedge (WW)]] ==Battle method== Matches were played using [[3on3 Battle]], in Hasbro's Xtreme Beystadium. The matches were first to 4 points, and the brackets were single elimination, following standard [[Beyblade Battle Base]] (B4) tournament structures. This was identical to the [[Beyblade X National Tournament (Canada)|rules and battle method used in the previous year]]. ==Trivia== ==External links== *[https://beyblade.com/gpfinal2026/ Official page (in English)] ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Tournaments]] [[Category:Official Tournaments]]

3rd place: [[DranSword 3-60F]] (Metal Coat: Bronze) |Champion=William |RunnerUp=[https://worldbeyblade.org/User-BelDaizora BelDaizora] |Date=August 16th, 2025[https://beyblade.com/worldchampionship2025/#regional World Championship 2025 official page] |Start=1:00 PM |Finish=4:00 PM |Length=3 hours }}The '''Beyblade X National Tournament''' was a Canadian regular-class tournament held on August 16th, 2025. The venue was [[wikipedia:Rogers Centre|Rogers Centre]], in Toronto, Ontario. The winners of the 8 regular-class regional tournaments held in June and July were given an all-expenses paid trip to this tournament. The winner of this tournament, William, was given an all-expenses paid trip to Tokyo, Japan to represent Canada at the [[Beyblade X World Championship 2025]]. ==Attendees== The 8 attendees were winners from the following regional tournaments: *Vancouver, BC (2 tournaments) *Toronto, ON *Saint-Jérôme, QC *Quebec City, QC *Dartmouth, NS *Orléans, ON *Calgary, AB For a total of 2 British Columbia, 2 Ontario, 2 Quebec, 1 Alberta and 1 Nova Scotia representatives. There were no representatives from the other 5 provinces of Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland, Prince Edward Island, and Saskatchewan, nor the 3 territories of Northwest Territories, Yukon, and Nunavut. ===Winning Combos=== *1st: William **TyrannoBeat 1-60R **WizardRod 9-60H **PhoenixWing 5-60T *2nd: BelDaizora **TyrannoRoar 5-60P **WizardRod 9-60B **PhoenixWing 9-60R ==Available Equipment== The equipment and rules of the national tournament were the same as the previously held regional tournaments, except [[3on3 Battle]] was exclusively played. Some regional tournaments only ran [[1on1 Battle]] during preliminaries, or throughout the entire tournament. All matches were played in Hasbro's [[Xtreme Beystadium]]. A legal products list was provided, which included some, but not all, of the Hasbro products available in Canada at the time. [[Takara Tomy]] products could not be used. ==Battle method== Matches were played using [[3on3 Battle]], in Hasbro's Xtreme Beystadium. The matches were first to 4 points, and the brackets were single elimination, following standard [[Beyblade Battle Base]] (B4) tournament structures. The ''Beyblade X'' regulations used were the 9th edition, released in Japan in July 2025. ==Trivia== ==External links== *[https://beyblade.com/worldchampionship2025/ Official page (in English)] ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Tournaments]] [[Category:Official Tournaments]]

October 12th, 2025 |Start=9:30 AM October 11th, 2025 |Finish=4:00 PM October 12th, 2025 |Length=2 days |Format=X }}The '''Beyblade X World Championship 2025''' was an international tournament that was held on October 11th and 12th, 2025, in Tokyo, Japan. The venue was RED° TOKYO TOWER, located at the base of [[wikipedia:Tokyo Tower|Tokyo Tower]]. Contrary to popular belief, the event was not managed by either [[Takara Tomy]] or [[Hasbro]], but rather by [[ADK Emotions Inc.]], the rights management company that handles the marketing and licensing of the ''Beyblade'' franchise. ==Qualifying Tournaments== *Winners of the national-level "X-Treme Cup GP 2025" and "Japan Championship 2025" Grand Prix tournaments would represent Japan in the open and regular-class tournaments. *The regional tournaments for Canada and the United States were held in partnership with Walmart.[https://i5.walmartimages.com/dfw/8822aef6-6814/k2-_d4cf4ecf-e2df-4263-9956-bef81f228694.v1.pdf&icid=cp_page_other_pov_card1_130895_4DBB0278A8 Walmart PDF] The regional tournaments were run by contractors hired by VIBRANT Marketing, a North American marketing firm based in Toronto.[https://www.instagram.com/reel/DLU87OWCr3v/ Instagram social media post] The Canadian national tournament was held in Toronto. *The regional tournaments in the United Kingdom were held in Smyths Toys Superstores across the country. ==Representatives== *Japan: Omanju King (Open Class) and Minato (Regular Class) *Korea: Yoo Ha Jun (Open Class) and Kim Jung U (Regular Class) *Taiwan: Jerry Yu (Open Class) and Hsu Jui Sheng (Regular Class) *China: Gan Hao (Open Class) and Zhu Tong Yu (Regular Class) *Hong Kong: Kyle (Open Class) and Adrian (Regular Class) *Singapore: Xavier (Open Class) and Aiman (Regular Class) *Malaysia: Akmal (Open Class) and Tang Jit An (Regular Class) *Philippines: Matt (Open Class) and Calvin (Regular Class) *Thailand: Yusin (Open Class) and Cannon (Regular Class) *Indonesia: Kurigura (Open Class) and Balya (Regular Class) *Türkiye: '''Fahreddin''' (Open Class) *USA: Elena Bey (Open Class) and Sebastian (Regular Class) *Canada: William (Regular Class) *Mexico: Ruan (Open Class) and '''Leobardo''' (Regular Class) *France: Berguiny (Regular Class) *Brazil: Marcelo (Regular Class) *Germany: Vivan (Regular Class) *Australia: Taylor (Open Class) and Thomas (Regular Class) *New Zealand: Charlie (Regular Class) *United Kingdom: Bleu (Regular Class) ==Available Equipment== All matches were played in the [[Xtreme Stadium]] (Hasbro: "Tournament Beystadium"). There were no banned products or parts during the tournament. Both [[Takara Tomy]] and [[Hasbro]] products released at the time could be used. Representatives from Asian countries received products containing parts that had not yet been released in Asia. For example, representatives from countries that had Takara Tomy distribution used the [[Blade - Hover Wyvern|Hover Wyvern]] Blade from the [[Drop Attack Battle Set]], which was only available from Hasbro at the time. Hover Wyvern saw a limited release in Japan two weeks later, as part of a DMM Lottery. This is contrary to qualifying tournaments elsewhere such as North America, which had an official legal products list (although this list was reportedly rarely followed). This is also in contrast to the past 4 World Championships, which also used ban lists that attempted to align with recent Hasbro releases. ==Battle method== Matches were played using [[3on3 Battle]], in the Xtreme Stadium. The matches were first to 4 points, and the brackets were single elimination, following standard [[Beyblade Battle Base]] (B4) tournament structures. The ''Beyblade X'' regulations used were the 10th edition, released in Japan in August 2025. ==Trivia== *As mentioned on the livestream, this was the first World Championship to take place in Japan, although it was not the first international tournament to take place in Japan. Several events, including the [[Asia Championship 2024]] held during the prior year, have taken place in Japan. ==External links == *[https://beyblade.com/worldchampionship2025/ Official page (in English)] *[https://beyblade.takaratomy.co.jp/worldchampionship/ Official page (in Japanese)] *[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l7c1DXN9kxA Announcement trailer (in English)] *[https://www.takaratomy.co.jp/english/product_release/pdf/p251012_en.pdf Takara Tomy Event Report Press Release (in English)] ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Tournaments]] [[Category:Official Tournaments]] [[Category:International Tournaments]] [[Category:World Championship]]

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Beystadium}} {{About|the Beyblade X stadium released in 2024|Beystadium (2026)|the stadium released in 2026 with the same name}} {{Product Infobox |Name=Beystadium |Image=XBS 2.jpeg |ProductCode=F9578 |ProductType=Stadium |Price=USD$12.99
CAD$16.99 |System=Basic Line |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseUS=June 1st, 2024 |ReleaseCA=May 30th, 2024 |ReleaseAU=May 16th, 2024 |XMasters=❌ |XStandard=❌ |XOpen=✔️ }}The '''Beystadium''' is a stadium released by [[Hasbro]] as part of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. It was released in western countries for USD$12.99 in the United States. ==Description== {{QuotePart |quote = The Beyblade X Beystadium introduces the X-Celerator Gear System. When the gears of the bit and rail of the stadium meet, tops rocket forward in an Xtreme Dash reaching intense speeds. |speaker = Official Description}} The '''Beystadium''' is a square "bucket" stadium with "X-Celerator Rails", a set of gears that interact with the gears on a Beyblade's [[Bit]] to activate the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. Unlike [[Takara Tomy]]'s [[Xtreme Stadium]] or Hasbro's [[Xtreme Beystadium]], the X-Celerator Rails are molded onto the stadium instead of being a separate component. A third Knockout Zone has been added to one of the stadium corners, for a total of 3 Knockout Zones and 1 Xtreme Finish Zone. parts.text:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Beystadium}}
{{About|the Beyblade X stadium released in 2026|Beystadium (2024)|the stadium released in 2024 with the same name}}

}}The '''Beystadium''' is a stadium released by [[Hasbro]] as part of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline.

==Description==
{{QuotePart
|quote=Features the X-Celerator Gear System innovation to level-up your game. When the gear of a Beyblade X top engages the rail of the stadium, it can super-accelerate into an Xtreme Dash rocketing it around the stadium for crushing collisions.
|speaker=Official Description}}
The '''Beystadium''' is a square "bucket" stadium with "X-Celerator Rails", a set of gears that interact with the gears on a Beyblade's [[Bit]] to activate the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. Unlike [[Takara Tomy]]'s [[Xtreme Stadium]] or Hasbro's [[Xtreme Beystadium]], the X-Celerator Rails are molded onto the stadium instead of being a separate component. A third Knockout Zone has been added to one of the stadium corners, for a total of 3 Knockout Zones and 1 Xtreme Finish Zone. Compared to the previous year's [[Beystadium (2024)|"bucket" stadium of the same name]], this release features redesigned corner walls in an attempt to address Beyblades easily exiting the previous model. The size, dimensions, and general design are otherwise nearly identical.

The X-Celerator Rails (and the gears) of the Xtreme Stadium/Beystadium are elevated due to being a separate part; as the '''Beystadium''' has these gears molded in, they are taller, extending to the stadium floor. Consequently, ''Gear'' Bits such as [[Bit - Gear Flat|Gear Flat (GF)]] will be able to use the [[Xtreme Dash]] more consistently, since the gears of the Bit extend to the stadium floor as well, making better contact with the X-Celerator Rails of the '''Beystadium'''. Bits with regular gears, especially Defense/Stamina Bits with more passive movement, may have difficulty using the Xtreme Dash.

Due to the additional Knockout Zone opposite to the Xtreme Finish Zone, and the smaller Battle Zone, the '''Beystadium''' heavily favors the use of Attack Type combinations, as Knockout/Xtreme Finishes are likely.

===Rulings===
Due to the lack of a stadium cover, Beyblades can easily exit the stadium, landing on the floor or hitting Bladers. As such, the [[World Beyblade Organization]] (WBO) does not allow the usage of the '''Beystadium''' in ranked tournaments.

G1669 (Hasbro) |Classification=Bit |Type=Balance |Weight=3.2 grams |System=Basic Line |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseJP=September 14th, 2024 |ReleaseUS=May 2025 |ReleaseCA=June 2025 |AttackStat=30 |DefenseStat=15 |StaminaStat=20 |DashStat=35 |BurstResistanceStat=30 |XStandard=✔️ }}{{Translation|'''Elevate'''|エレベート|Erebēto}} is a [[Bit]] released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the [[Basic Line]] system. It debuted in Japan with the release of the BX-36 [[Random Booster WhaleWave Select]] on September 14th, 2024. It later debuted in western countries with the release of [[Hasbro]]'s Booster Pack, [[Tide Whale 5-80E]]. ==Description== '''Elevate''' or '''E''' is a Balance Type Bit that features a flat tip with a bump protruding in the center, and a large disc surrounding it. The wide ring is intended to 'elevate' the Bit above the Stadium floor during an [[Xtreme Dash]], preventing Stamina loss. The elevated Bit also allows an '''Elevate''' combo to more easily do [[Smash Attack]]s with an Xtreme Dash. The smooth perimeter of the ring also provides Life-After-Death (LAD) potential. This LAD allows an '''Elevate''' combo to roll on the disc when tilted or swaying at the end of a battle. Although it is a Balance Type Bit, '''Elevate''' has a weak Burst Lock (low Burst Resistance) shaft that is usually found on Stamina Type Bits. This was done to balance its high performance.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ihhz4b_B36M WhaleWave official video] Upon release, '''Elevate''' quickly became prominently used with the [[Blade - CobaltDragoon|CobaltDragoon]] Blade that had been released 2 months earlier. At the time Cobalt Dragoon had not yet become prominent in the metagame, with Bladers experimenting with Bits such as [[Bit - Glide|Glide (G)]] to achieve mixed results in Opposite-Spin Stamina matchups. With '''Elevate''', the combo [[Blade - CobaltDragoon|CobaltDragoon]] [[Ratchet - 5-60|5-60]][[Bit - Elevate|E]] became a popular counterpick to the popular [[Blade - WizardRod|WizardRod]] [[Ratchet - 3-60|3-60]][[Bit - Ball|B]] combo, which had been frequently used in tournaments. Unlike previous Cobalt Dragoon combos, combos utilizing '''Elevate''' were able to destabilize the opponent's [[Blade - WizardRod|WizardRod]] [[Ratchet - 3-60|3-60]][[Bit - Ball|B]] combo when launched correctly. The combo was also recommended by Takara Tomy in several publications, including the [[CoroCoro Comic]] magazine and the inserts included with the [[Random Booster WhaleWave Select]]. This combo also saw usage during the [[Asia Championship 2024]] and the qualification tournaments preceding it. ==Overall== ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== * BX-36 [[Random Booster WhaleWave Select]] - 01: [[WhaleWave 5-80E]] * BX-48 [[Random Booster Vol. 9]] - 02: [[SharkEdge 4-70E]] * BX-00 [[MammothTusk 2-80E]] * CX-00 [[Evangelion Deck Set]] - [[EvaArc B0-70E]] (Unit-00 Version) * UX-12 [[Random Booster Vol. 5]] - 04: [[LeonClaw 0-80E]] ===Hasbro=== * G1669 [[Tide Whale 5-80E]] * G3061 [[Grogu and Snowtrooper Multipack Set]] - [[Grogu 3-85E]] ==Gallery== BitElevatePrototype.png|Elevate (BX-36; Initial Prototype) BitElevate.png|Elevate (BX-36; Second Prototype) Elevate (BX-00).png|Elevate (BX-00) Elevate (Grogu).png|Elevate (G3061) ==Trivia== *The original Attack Type design of '''Elevate''' had a decagonal guard instead of a disk, and no bump protruding from the bottom, creating a wide flat tip. {{About|Gear Point|Bit - Point|its normal counterpart}} {{Part Infobox |Image=BitGearPoint.png |Name=Gear Point |JPName=ギヤポイント |RomajiName=Giya Pointo |AKA=GP |ProductCode=BX-26 (Takara Tomy)
G0283 (Hasbro) |Classification=Bit |Type=Balance |Weight=2.3 grams |System=Basic Line |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseJP=January 27th, 2024 |ReleaseUS=July 27th, 2024 |ReleaseCA=August 29th, 2024 |AttackStat=30 |DefenseStat=25 |StaminaStat=15 |DashStat=30 |BurstResistanceStat=80 |XStandard=✔️ }}{{Translation|'''Gear Point'''|ギヤポイント|Giya Pointo}} is a [[Bit]] released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the [[Basic Line]] system. It debuted in Japan with the release of the BX-26 Booster, [[UnicornSting 5-60GP]], on January 27th, 2024. It later debuted in western countries with the release of [[Hasbro]]'s Booster Pack, [[Sting Unicorn 5-60GP]]. ==Description== '''Gear Point''' or '''GP''' is a Balance Type Bit that features a flat tip with the gears intended for the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick extending to the bottom of the tip. The result is a twelve-pointed wide flat tip, and like the regular [[Bit - Point|Point]] Bit, a small ball protrudes from the center. The performance of '''Gear Point''' varies depending on the angle it is launched at; when tilted and launched at an angle, the flat tip creates extremely aggressive movement, which makes it easier to contact the Xtreme Line (X-Celerator Rail) to perform the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. When launched horizontally, parallel to the Stadium floor, a '''Gear Point''' combination will stay in the center of the Stadium, creating high Stamina. However, even if it is launched parallel, when knocked off balance a '''Gear Point''' combination will revert to the aggressive movement of the flat tip, draining Stamina. '''Gear Point''' is essentially a fusion of the [[Bit - Gear Flat|Gear Flat]] and Point Bits. The general shape is identical to Gear Flat with the addition of the protruding ball instead of a circular indent. Consequently, its tilted Attack movement is nearly identical to that of Gear Flat's. Its general usage is similar to that of Point, but '''Gear Point''' offers more speed and aggressive movement than Point when tilted, at the cost of higher Stamina drain. ==Overall== ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== * BX-26 [[UnicornSting 5-60GP]] * BX-39 [[Random Booster ShelterDrake Select]] - 01: [[ShelterDrake 7-80GP]] * BX-00 [[DranDagger 2-80GP]] (Giants Version) * BX-00 [[SharkEdge 2-60GP]] (Fishing Spirits Wonder Ver.) * BX-00 [[BBLD Booster]] - 03: [[UnicornSting 5-60GP]] (Pink-BBLD) * UX-05 [[Random Booster ShinobiShadow Select]] - 03: [[ShinobiShadow 3-70GP]] ===Hasbro=== * G0283 [[Sting Unicorn 5-60GP]] * G1675 [[Shelter Drake 7-80GP]] * G2733 [[Gust Bat 3-85GP]] * G3393 [[Yggdrasil Team Pack]] - [[Sting Unicorn 5-60GP]] ==Gallery== BitGearPoint.png|Gear Point (BX-26/G0283/G3393) ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Basic Line Parts}} [[Category:Takara Tomy]] [[Category:Hasbro]]

G0842 (Hasbro) |Classification=Bit |Type=Attack |Weight=1.9 grams |System=Unique Line |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseJP=December 28th, 2024 |ReleaseUS=May 2025 |ReleaseCA=May 2025 |ReleaseAU=May 2025 |AttackStat=45 |DefenseStat=5 |StaminaStat=15 |DashStat=35 |BurstResistanceStat=80 |XStandard=✔️ }}{{Translation|'''Low Rush'''|ローラッシュ|Rō Rasshu}} is a [[Bit]] released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the [[Unique Line]] system. It debuted in Japan with the release of the UX-11 Starter, [[ImpactDrake 9-60LR]], on December 28th, 2024. It later debuted in western countries with the release of [[Hasbro]]'s [[Drop Attack Battle Set]]. ==Description== '''Low Rush''' or '''LR''' is an Attack Type Bit that features a flat tip that creates aggressive movement, which makes it easier to contact the Xtreme Line (X-Celerator Rail) to perform the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. '''Low Rush''' is a shorter variant of [[Bit - Rush|Rush (R)]], and is about 1 millimeter shorter. Like its regular counterpart, '''Low Rush''' has a smaller diameter tip and less gears than other flat Bits. The fewer gears mean less Stamina is used when contact is made with the Xtreme Line when an Xtreme Dash is performed. However, a consequence is having a slower Xtreme Dash, although this is intended to increase the frequency of Xtreme Dashes, hence its name - "Rush" [Attacks]. The lower height of '''Low Rush''' also makes it easier for a combo to perform [[Upper Attack]]s. The ring around the Bit has three indents to indicate it is a Low-type Bit. G2754 (Hasbro) |Classification=Bit |Type=Balance |Weight=3.4 grams |System=Basic Line |Series=Beyblade X (Season 2) |ReleaseJP=August 9th, 2025 |ReleaseUS=January 30th, 2026 |ReleaseCA=February 12th, 2026 |AttackStat=50 |DefenseStat=20 |StaminaStat=10 |DashStat=20 |BurstResistanceStat=80 |XStandard=✔️ }}{{Translation|'''Merge'''|マージ|Māji}} is a [[Bit]] released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the [[Basic Line]] system. It debuted in Japan with the release of the BX-45 Booster, [[SamuraiCalibur 6-70M]], on August 9th, 2025. It later debuted in western countries with the release of [[Hasbro]]'s [[Calibur Samurai and Obsidian Shell Dual Pack]]. ==Description== '''Merge''' or '''M''' is a Balance Type Bit that features a flat rubber tip, with a plastic sharp tip protruding from the center. When '''Merge''' is knocked off balance by an opponent or launched at an angle, the outer rubber tip will contact the stadium floor, creating aggressive movement. When launched parallel to the stadium floor, the '''Merge''' combo will spin on the plastic sharp, and go back to the center of the stadium. '''Merge''' is the first Bit to feature 18 gears instead of the standard 12, increasing the speed of a '''Merge''' combo's Xtreme Dash, at the cost of Stamina. '''Merge''' is also 4 millimeter taller than the standard Bit height, with taller gears and a larger area between the gears and the area that contacts the Ratchet of the combo. Due to the additional height, '''Merge''' is also the heaviest Bit at its release, being slightly heavier than Elevate, which was previously the heaviest Bit. Like Elevate, '''Merge''' appears to have undergone several revisions to its design; the [[SamuraiCalibur 6-70M]] product renders released by [[Takara Tomy]] and [[Hasbro]] display a '''Merge''' prototype at a standard height. Coincidentally, these renders also show [[WhaleWave 5-80E]] with the original Elevate prototype design. ==Overall== ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== * BX-45 [[SamuraiCalibur 6-70M]] * BX-00 [[StormSpriggan 2-70M]] ===Hasbro=== * G2754 [[Calibur Samurai and Obsidian Shell Dual Pack]] - [[Calibur Samurai 6-70M]] ==Gallery== BitMerge.png|Merge (Initial Prototype) Merge (BX-00).png|Merge (BX-00) ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Basic Line Parts}} [[Category:Takara Tomy]] [[Category:Hasbro]]

The flat tip creates aggressive movement, which results in easy contact with the Xtreme Line (X-Celerator Rail) to perform the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. Compared to its predecessor [[Bit - Flat|Flat]], '''Rush''' has a smaller diameter tip and less gears. This results in less Stamina being used when contact is made with the Xtreme Line and an Xtreme Dash occurs. However, a consequence is having a slower Xtreme Dash, although this is intended to increase the frequency of Xtreme Dashes, hence its name "Rush" [Attacks]. ==Overall== A staple part since its release, '''Rush''' provides top-tier Attack performance, without some of the self-destructive risks of more aggressive Attack Type Bits. Due to the smaller tip diameter and reduction in gears, '''Rush''' has the highest Stamina performance of all Attack Type Bits. Furthermore, '''Rush''' has use in [[Anti-Attack]] combinations, such as ones utilizing the [[Blade - WizardRod|WizardRod]] Blade. ==Description==
{{QuotePart
|quote = The Wedge Bit's angled tip is now surrounded by a cylindrical wall, further reducing tilting.
|speaker = Official Description}}
<onlyinclude>'''Wall Wedge''' or '''WW''' is a Defense Type Bit that is a variant of the standard [[Bit - Wedge|Wedge]] Bit. It has added the same "wall" design previously seen with the [[Bit - Wall Ball|Wall Ball (WB)]] Bit, which is intended to reduce tilting by pushing the Bey upright when the wall touches the stadium floor. '''Wall Wedge''' retains the same small diameter sharp tip as Wedge, which generates high Stamina, and settles in the center of the stadium. Unlike Wedge, which had a decreased 10-tooth gear instead of the standard 12, '''Wall Wedge''' instead has a 16-tooth gear. Having additional teeth increases the speed of an Xtreme Dash at the cost of Stamina. As '''Wall Wedge''' is intended to be a Defense-type Bit, this is not desirable on a standard Defense combo. However, on [[Anti-Attack]] combos, this may be used to increase its Attack potential.</onlyinclude>

parts.text:
{{Part Infobox |Image=BladeAeroPegasus.png |Name=AeroPegasus |JPName=エアロペガサス |RomajiName=EaroPegasasu |ProductCode=UX-00 |Classification=Blade |Type=Attack |SpinDirection=Right-Spin |Weight=38.2 grams (first mold)
38.7 grams (second mold) |System=Basic Line |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseJP=July 30th, 2024 |AttackStat=60 |DefenseStat=25 |StaminaStat=30 |XStandard=✔️ }}{{Translation|'''AeroPegasus'''|エアロペガサス|EaroPegasasu}} is a [[Blade]] released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the [[Unique Line]] system. It debuted in Japan with the release of the UX-00 Rare Bey Get Battle Prize Booster, [[AeroPegasus 3-70A]], on July 30th, 2024. ==Description== '''AeroPegasus''' is a three-sided Attack Type Blade with three curved upward slanting contact points. '''AeroPegasus''' is a reference to Beyblades from ''[[Metal Fight Beyblade]]'', in this case being the Pegasis line of Beyblades. The Gear Chip features the side profile of [[wikipedia:Pegasus|Pegasus]], a winged horse from Greek mythology and one of the 88 constellations in space. The Gear Chip has a diamond/hexagonal shape in the background that references "Face" parts from the ''Metal Fight Beyblade'' toyline. The three sides create excellent [[Upper Attack]] and [[Smash Attack]]. '''AeroPegasus''' features six "air duct" holes, which are intended to improve aerodynamic performance by reducing drag from air moving through the holes. As part of the ''[[Unique Line]]'', '''AeroPegasus''' has resin Launcher Hooks instead of metal ones, which increase Outward Weight Distribution (OWD). The Unique Line gimmick of '''AeroPegasus''' was initially advertised by Takara Tomy as its "Double Metal Coat", referring to the original release's use of blue and green paint. The ''Red Version'' release simply removes any mention of the Double Metal Coat. At the time of its release, was the heaviest Blade available, heavier than [[Blade - CobaltDrake|CobaltDrake]] and [[Blade - PhoenixWing|PhoenixWing]], which both weighed 38.0 grams on average. However, '''AeroPegasus''' was surpassed by the [[Blade - ImpactDrake|ImpactDrake]] Blade, 5 months later. Despite being outclassed in weight, '''AeroPegasus''' has a superior shape and is heavier than most Defense and Stamina Blades. '''AeroPegasus''' is highly versatile in Attack combinations, and can be used on flat Bits such as [[Bit - Low Flat|Low Flat (LF)]], [[Bit - Low Rush|Low Rush (LR)]], and [[Bit - Level|Level (L)]]. At the time of writing, '''AeroPegasus''' has been a staple part in [[Beyblade Battle Base|B4]] and [[WBO]] tournaments since its release. Releases of '''AeroPegasus''' produced during January 2026 onward have a new reinforced mold that is heavier by 0.5 grams on average. This second mold was first released with the ''Red Version''. ==Overall== The heavy weight and excellent Attack capabilities of '''AeroPegasus''' make it a staple Blade. '''As such, AeroPegasus is a must-have for the WBO's X format.''' ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== *BX-53 [[All In One Set]] - [[AeroPegasus 3-70A]] (Double Metal Coat: Blue×Cyan) *UX-00 [[AeroPegasus 3-70A]] (Double Metal Coat: Blue×Green) ([[Rare Bey Get Battle]]) *UX-00 [[AeroPegasus 3-70A]] (Red Version) ==Gallery== BladeAeroPegasus.png|AeroPegasus (Double Metal Coat: Blue×Green) Aero Pegasus (Red Version).jpg|AeroPegasus (Red Version) ==Trivia== *While Metal Coat releases typically add 5 to the Attack, Defense, and Stamina stats, the Double Metal Coat: Blue×Green release adds 10 to the Attack stat instead of 5. This is possibly due to the "Double Metal Coat" classification. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Unique Line Parts}} [[Category:Takara Tomy]] [[Category:Takara Tomy Exclusives]] [[Category:Parts with multiple molds]]

It debuted in western countries with the release of the [[Bite Croc and Sting Unicorn Dual Pack]]. It later debuted in Japan as {{Translation|'''CrocoCrunch'''|クロコクランチ|KurokoKuranchi}} with the release of the BX-00 mail order Booster, [[CrocoCrunch 2-60Q]], on January 15th, 2025. ==Description== '''Bite Croc''' (Japanese: '''CrocoCrunch''') is an Attack Type Blade with two large blades acting as the main contact points. The Gear Chip features a [[wikipedia:Crocodile|crocodile]]. The two large blades have very aggressive shapes, producing a massive amount of [[Smash Attack]]. They are also sloped upwards to produce [[Upper Attack]]. '''CrocoCrunch''' is a retool of [[Blade - SharkEdge|SharkEdge (Keel Shark)]]; the plastic components are identical, and the metal component is nearly identical. Texturing resembling a crocodile has been added to the two large blades, but otherwise has remained unchanged. Compared to SharkEdge, '''CrocoCrunch''' weighs slightly less, averaging half a gram lighter. As such, there is no advantage in using '''CrocoCrunch''' over the heavier SharkEdge and [[Blade - Optimus Primal|Optimus Primal]], another SharkEdge retool, although the difference in performance is minor. Compared to other retools, '''CrocoCrunch''' and Optimus Primal have the least differences with their design base, SharkEdge. ==Overall== ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== *BX-00 [[CrocoCrunch 2-60Q]] (Metal Coat: Green) ===Hasbro=== *G0199 [[Bite Croc and Sting Unicorn Dual Pack]] - [[Bite Croc 3-60LF]] *G3083 [[Bite Croc Deluxe String Launcher & Custom Grip Set]] - [[Bite Croc 2-60Q]] (Metal Coat: Green) ==Gallery== Bite Croc 3-60LF.jpeg|Bite Croc (G0198) ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Basic Line Parts}} [[Category:Hasbro]] [[Category:Takara Tomy]]
