He fights with his Beyblade, [[BrachioWhip OW5-70Nr|Whip Brachio OW 5-70Nr]]. ==Appearance== Six is a tall male with a muscular build, He has black/grey hair and blue eyes he has a purple headband with a blue crisscross pattern. He wears a white tank top with the [[Cross Corporation]] logo and blue pants, a purple jacket wraped around his waist, and blue sneakers with purple lances and light grey soles. In the past, before improving his launch power, Six was average height. He wore a magenta jacket with a white hoodie and white stripes on the sleeves, that he wore unzipped and with the Cross Corporation logo on the back of the jacket. Underneath his jacket, he wears a black shirt, a pair of grey pants, and indigo sneakers. ==Personality== Just like other members of the Cross Family, Six is very arrogant when it comes to his own skills, believing no one can match him when it comes to launch power and technique. In his past, Six lacked confidence in himself, only gaining some when Zero encouraged him to train and increase his launch power. Despite his confidence, when Six is put into a position that may result in him losing, as seen during his battle with [[Robin Kazami|Robin]], Six somewhat reverts back to his old less confident personality, choosing to running away instead of seeing the battle through to its end. ==Biography== ===Background=== Six Cross is one of the children of [[Zero Cross]] in the expansive Cross family. He was once widely regarded as the weakest Blader among his siblings, lacking natural talent and even appearing weaker than some of the younger ones such as Nine at times. Flashbacks show him enduring taunts from siblings like Three and Four, though others would offered some support or encouragement. His major turning point came when Zero Cross gave him a prototype of the Whip Brachio (later refined into his signature Whip Brachio OW 5-70Nr). Zero instructed him to focus narrowly on improving his shooting power. Six took this directive to heart, practicing tirelessly day and night. Through dedication, he targeted refinements on his launch form and movements, and transformed dramatically. He rose from the bottom of the family hierarchy to become one of the strongest Bladers in the Cross Clan—achieving the strongest launch power among his siblings, even surpassing [[One Cross]]. According to Nine, he is now among the most skillful, though he remains reclusive and rarely shows himself.''[[Beyblade X (Season 3)|Beyblade X]]'' Episode 124, ''[[Beyblade X - Episode 124|True X Tower War]]''[[Beyblade X (Season 3)|''Beyblade X'']] Chapter 35, [[Beyblade X - Chapter 35|''The Best Battle In History'']] [[Beyblade X (Season 3)|''Beyblade X'']] [[Beyblade X - Chapter 36|Chapter 36]]''[[Beyblade X (Season 3)|Beyblade X]]'' Episode 129, ''[[Beyblade X - Episode 129|Natural Talent]]'' ===''[[Beyblade X]]''=== ==Beyblades== * '''[[BrachioWhip OW5-70Nr|Whip Brachio OW 5-70Nr]]''': Six's Custom Line Expand Blade Beyblade in [[Beyblade X (Season 3)|''Beyblade X'']]. He was originally given a prototype version of the Beyblade until it was refined into the Whip Brachio today. ===Generic/Borrowed Beys=== *'''[[RhinoHorn 3-80GB|Horn Rhino 3-80GB]]''': Six's Basic Line Beyblade prior to obtaining Whip Brachio in the anime. ===Special Moves=== *{{Special Move|Hyper Boost Jurassic Titan}} ==Beybattles== ===Anime=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X (Season 3) |- !Opponent !Episode !Result |- |[[Robin Kazami]] |[[Beyblade X - Episode 129|129]] |Lose |- |[[Five Cross]] |129 (flashback) |Win |- |[[Eight Cross]] |129 (flashback) |Win |- |[[Three Cross|Three]] and [[Four Cross]] |129 (flashback) |Win |} ===Manga=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X |- !Opponent !Chapter !Result |- |[[Robin Kazami]] |[[Beyblade X - Chapter 36|36]] |Lose |} ==Official Descriptions== The sixth brother of the Cross family. Lacking talent for Beyblade, he was once considered the weakest of his siblings. However, after being ordered by Zero Cross to "simply train your shooting power," he tirelessly practiced shooting day and night, eventually achieving the strongest level of shooting power among his siblings. It is included with the [[Sneak Attack Battle Set]]. ==Description== {{QuotePart |quote = A new stadium that adds a pop-up rail alongside the signature X-Celerator Rail. |speaker = Official Description}} The '''Sneak Attack Beystadium''' is the sixth [[Hasbro]]-exclusive Beystadium in the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. It was released as part of the [[Sneak Attack Battle Set]], Hasbro's stadium set for 2026. The '''Sneak Attack Beystadium''' features a rectangular design and an "X-Celerator Rail", a set of gears that interact with the gears on a Beyblade's [[Bit]] to activate the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. Like the [[Drop Attack Beystadium]] from the year before, the gears of the X-Celerator Rails are molded in, extending to the stadium floor. The titular "sneak attack" is possible with the addition of a "pop-up rail" at the end of the "X-Celerator Rail". Unlike all previous ''Beyblade X'' stadiums, the pocket layout has been changed, with a wide 3 point "Xtreme Finish Zone" at the front of the stadium, and 2 point "Knockout Zones" in the two back corners. ==Dimensions== ==Gallery== Sneak Attack Beystadium Gimmick.jpeg|Sneak Attack Beystadium's gimmick ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Hasbro Exclusives]]

She fights alongside her ''Samurai'' Beyblades and is introduced in the second season as the fourth and newest member of [[Persona]], the protagonist team of the series, vowing to defeat her mother, [[Omega Shiroboshi]]. Following the title match with [[Zodiac]], Tenka would leave the team to continue being an instructor at the [[Shiroboshi School]]. ==Appearance== Tenka is a girl of average height, with black and violet hair that she has tied in a ponytail, has violet eyes, and a mark of a white star on her forehead. She wears a hakama attire with three white stars outline with purple, on the top marked with a green "X" on it. Like her mother, Tenka possesses triangular teeth. On occasions, she would wear a white hoodie with a purple star over her hakama attire. In the Triple Battle, adopting the alter ego of Blader S, her mask is a dark red with a black lens with a gear-shaped pattern on the lens, and a pink "S" at the center of the lens, and a red bean cream sushi is decorated on top of the mask. When she was a young child, her attire consited of a white shirt with black rims and magenta shorts. During her training in the Shiroboshi School, she wore a white hakama attire with a white and green hair tie. ==Personality== When Tenka made her first appearance, she came off as a rude and disrespectful, calling Robin too weak to be a pro, and insulting Multi’s skills both as a blader and Beycrafter. The only one Tenka seemed to respect was Jaxon, but only because she wanted to use him to defeat her mother, Omega. In her "Meet the Bladers" video she was said to be brash, calculating and brutally honest. Tenka’s time with Persona changed her opinion about them, realizing that friendship helps keep the team together. Tenka also realized the important role that both Robin and Multi play that makes Persona strong. Like most bladers, Tenka always gives any battle her best effort regardless if her opponent is a newbie or a pro. This mostly likely stems from Tenka’s training at the Shiroboshi School, believing that not giving it her all is not only disrespectful to herself, but also her opponents. ==Biography== ===Background=== Tenka is an instructor of the [[Shiroboshi School]]. She was later revealed to be the daughter of [[Omega Shiroboshi]], Tenka was sent after her mother who broke the dojo's rule of Shiroboshi Style practitioners of participating in the [[The X|X Tower]]. ===''Beyblade X''=== ==Beyblades== ===Primary Beys=== *'''[[SamuraiSteel 5-70GF|Steel Samurai 5-70GF]]''': Tenka's Attack Type Basic Line Beyblade in the ''Beyblade X'' manga. It is a Shiroboshi School heirloom that is passed down to each new head instructor. While the Bey does not make an appearance in the manga itself, a checklist in the October 2025 issue of the [[CoroCoro Comic]] magazine shows Tenka as the current owner. *'''[[SamuraiSaber 2-70L|Saber Samurai 2-70L]]''': Tenka's Attack Type Unique Line Beyblade in ''[[Beyblade X (Season 2)|Beyblade X]]''. It is a Shiroboshi School heirloom that is passed down to each new head instructor. *'''[[SamuraiCalibur 6-70M|Calibur Samurai 6-70M]]''': Tenka's Balance Type Basic Line Beyblade in ''Beyblade X''. }}'''The X''', known as the {{Translation|'''X Tower'''|{{Ruby|X|エックス}}タワー|Ekkusu Tawā}} in Japan, is a location in the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' anime and manga. The 2 towers are named {{Translation|'''Slash Tower'''|スラッシュタワー|Surasshu Tawā}} and {{Translation|'''Solidus Tower'''|ソリダスタワー|Soridasu Tawā}}.<ref name="XC015" />

==Appearance==
The X features 100 floors in both towers. The Slash Tower and the Solidus Tower intersect to form an "X", hence the name of the tower. On the 100th floors, the ceiling can be opened up during the title match.

==Biography==
Located in [[Xenon City]], '''The X''' serves as the gathering place for Pro Bladers who are part of the [[Pro League]].<ref name="XC001">''[[Beyblade X]]'' Chapter 1, ''[[Beyblade X - Chapter 01|X]]''</ref> There are 2 towers and 100 total floors in each tower.<ref name="XC006">''[[Beyblade X]]'' Chapter 6, ''[[Beyblade X - Chapter 06|Kadovar's Test]]''</ref><ref name="XC015">''[[Beyblade X]]'' Chapter 15, ''[[Beyblade X - Chapter 15|Battle at the Top (Part 3)]]''</ref> The final and 100th floor is known as '''The Peak''' (Japanese: '''The Top'''), where the current champions can be challenged.

Between the two towers, the '''Slash Tower''' favor flashy battle styles focusing on Xtreme Dashes and high ratings from the audience while the '''Solidus Tower''' strives for strength and the fundamentals, exalting Survivor Finishes above all others. However, Pro Bladers transferring between both towers are allowed to continue from the same floor as previous.<ref name="X064">''[[Beyblade X]]'' Episode 67, ''[[Beyblade X - Episode 67|Formless Shadow]]''</ref>

==Teams==

===Solidus Tower===

*[[Zodiac]]

==Events==
*This is where teams at similar floors battle against each other to advance to a higher floor.
* This is where Pro Bladers must pass [[Beyblade X - Episode 11|Warden's Test]] to advance to the upper floors of the tower by beating or outlasting [[Warden]]'s [[WyvernGale 5-80GB|Gale Wyvern 5-80GB]] under 30 seconds.
*This is where the Shuffle Battle Fest is held, with the first place team in the team votes battle against Team Dreams which consists of the top 3 bladers from the individual vote before advancing to the Title Match.
*This is where exhibition matches are held.
*This is where the title match against the champion team is held at the 100th floor of the tower.
*This is where the champion teams from both Slash Tower and Solidus Tower are able to challenge each other for the overall champion at the X.

He fights with his Beyblade, [[SolEclipse D5-70TK|Umbra Sol D 5-70TK]], which is shared with his twin sister, [[Four Cross]]. ==Appearance== Three is a tall, tan-skinned male with heterochromia eyes, with his left eye being orange and right eye being purple, and he has orange wavy hair with purple streaks. He also has two moles above and below his left eye. Like his twin sister, he wears a grey jacket with white collar, a black undershirt and a pair of white shorts, but with orange linings, long black tights, a sun necklace and a pair of dark grey shoes with orange laces. He also occasionally wears an orange long-sheeved jacket with the [[Cross Corporation]] logo. He often carries a small pouch with Four that holds their Beyblade, Umbra Sol. ==Personality== Due to his talent in blading, Three has shown to be quite arrogant and haughty, often mocking opponents he believes to be weaker than him. This extends to some of his siblings, especially Nine and Six. And due to this, he never changed his tactics, which would be his mistake during his rematch against Sigrid, who is now familiar with Umbra Sol's weakness. Like Four, he does not take kindly to people saying that he is only strong because of his twin sister. Like his other siblings, Three is also desperately trying to win his father's approval, fearing Zero might abandon him if he loses. ==Biography== ===Background=== Three is one of the nine children of [[Zero Cross]] of the Cross Clan and is also the twin brother of [[Four Cross]], having seven other siblings who are all talented in blading. But amongst the clan there's an open secret amongst the family of a 10th secret child whose identity is unknown. He would later be witness to his father's plan to destroy and save [[Xenon City]]'s blading profession from destruction. ===''Beyblade X''=== ==Beyblades== ===Primary Beys=== *'''[[SolEclipse D5-70TK|Umbra Sol D 5-70TK]]''': Three's Custom Line Beyblade in ''Beyblade X'', which he shares with Four, exclusively using its Double Uppercut Mode. He and Four would later each use identical copies of Umbra Sol. ===Generic/Replica Beys=== *'''[[TyrannoBeat 3-60T|Beat Tyranno 3-60T]]''': Three's Basic Line Beyblade prior to obtaining Umbra Sol. *'''[[OrochiCluster 6-60LF|Coil Orochi 6-60LF]]''': A Unique Line Beyblade that was created by [[Zero Cross]] and completed by [[Five Cross]] to stop [[Jaxon Cross]] from battling [[Khrome Ryugu]]. ===Special Moves=== * {{Special Move|Xtreme Dash}} ** Umbra Sol's Xtreme Dash uses the suffix "Solar Burst". In its Double Uppercut Mode, Umbra Sol uses its 5 upper blades to attack from below, launching the opponent upwards and resulting in a Burst Finish. This Special Move is often used in tandem with Four's [[Hyper Boost Solar Void]] as a pincer attack or to divert the opponent towards Three's Umbra Sol. ** Coil Orochi's Xtreme Dash uses the suffix "Yamata no Orochi". After destabilizing the opponent rapid "poisonous" strikes, it lands the final strike by combing two of its snake-headed blades. This Special Move in tadem with Four's Xtreme Dash Yamata no Orochi, both Coil Orochi ram into the opposing Beyblade with combined force and power. ==Beybattles== ===Anime=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X (Season 3) |- !Opponent !Episode !Result |- |[[Ginro]] (with [[Four Cross]]) |[[Beyblade X - Episode 104|104]] |Win (4-2) |- |[[Titus Manju]] |[[Beyblade X - Episode 105|105]] |Win |- |[[Jaxon Cross]] (with Four Cross) |[[Beyblade X - Episode 106|106]] |Lose |- |[[Sigrid Nana-iro]] (with Four Cross) |[[Beyblade X - Episode 111|111]] |Lose |- |[[Nine Cross]] (with Four Cross) |[[Beyblade X - Episode 120|120]] |Win (3-0) |- |[[Million Mizu]] (with Four Cross) |120-[[Beyblade X - Episode 121|121]] |Lose |- |[[Six Cross]] (with Four Cross) |[[Beyblade X - Episode 129|129]] |Lose |} ===Manga=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X |- !Opponent !Episode !Result |- |[[Ginro]] (with [[Four Cross]]) |[[Beyblade X - Chapter 29|29]] |Win |- |[[Jaxon Cross]] (with Four Cross) |[[Beyblade X - Chapter 30|30]] |Lose (0-3) |} ==Official Descriptions== The third sibling of the Kurosu Clan and the older twin brother of Four Kurosu. He has long nails, whisker tattoos on his face and very prominent fangs. His hair resembles a mane of a lion and his outfits represent african tribes. His attire consists of a black shirt, a brown sleeveless fur-trimmed jacket, a necklace with three sharp fangs, a pair of black and yellow wristbands, brown shorts, a belt with a crest depicting a lion and black boots with grey soles. ==Personality== Although Titus proclaims himself as king, he is not a tyrant, but is a kind person who is loyal to his teammates, Toguro and Jian, whom he trusts in their blading skills. He also takes good care of the animals at Lion's Jungle, especially Shishimaru the Lion. ==Biography== ===Background=== Titus is a member of the 3-person team [[Zooganic]]. [[Beybattle Pass]] |JpVoice=Yuki Terui |EnVoice=Joshua Waters |AppearAnime=[[Beyblade X - Episode 65|First Flight]] (flashback) |AppearManga= }}'''Tsubasa Takaya''', known as {{Translation|'''Tsubasa Takano'''|鷹野ツバサ|Takano Tsubasa}} in Japan, is a character appearing in the ''[[Beyblade X (Season 2)|Beyblade X]]'' anime. His Beyblade is [[WyvernGale 5-80GB|Gale Wyvern 5-80GB]]. ==Appearance== Tsubasa appears to be an average height teenage boy. He has dark gray eyes and long moss green colored hair which is tied into a low ponytail and has swept bangs on his forehead. He has an ahoge on top of his head and his hair appears to be slighlty messy. He wears an aquamarine denim jacket with pastel yellow buttoned up dress and an orange pendant. He also wears navy blue skinny jeans and pastel yellow loafers. ==Personality== Despite being naturally quiet, Tsubasa is incredibly supportive of his peers. When Robin Kazami initially rejects his offer to try Blading, Tsubasa doesn't push aggressively; instead, he gently creates a welcoming space that eventually inspires Robin—and later their whole class—to discover the joy of the sport. He possesses a deeply giving nature. Rather than hoarding his rare or personal spinning tops, he openly shares his collection and even gives Robin his ''Strike Hawk'' Beyblade just to spark his friend's interest. Because of the immense pressure from his overprotective mother, Tsubasa exhibits a strong sense of anxious compliance. He struggles to stand up for his own desires and initially submits to her rigid demands for strict professional training, showing that he can be easily overwhelmed by parental authority. He starts off quite shy and reserved when he transfers to a new school, but quickly shows a gentle and kind-hearted nature toward his peers. ==Biography== ===Background=== ===''Beyblade X''=== ==Beyblades== *'''[[WyvernGale 5-80GB|Gale Wyvern 5-80GB]]''': Tsubasa's primary Basic Line Beyblade in ''Beyblade X''. ===Special Moves=== *{{Special Move|Xtreme Dash}} **Tsubasa's Gale Wyvern uses the suffixes "Swallow Flip". Using the momentum from the opponent and rides near the end of the "Xtreme Line" of the Xtreme Stadium. *{{Special Move|True Swallow Flip}} ==Beybattles== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X (Season 2) |- !Opponent !Episode !Result |- |[[Suzaki]] |[[Beyblade X - Episode 65|65]] (flashback) |Win |- |Unknown Blader |65 (flashback) |Win |- |Cleo Cle |[[Beyblade X - Episode 66|66]] (flashback) |Win (2-0) |- |[[Robin Kazami]] |66 (flashback) |Lose (0-3) |} ==Anime Appearances== ===[[Beyblade X (Season 2)]]=== * [[Beyblade X - Episode 65|''Episode 65 - First Flight'']] (flashback) * [[Beyblade X - Episode 66|''Episode 66 - Something Captivating'']] (flashback) ==Relationships== ==Gallery== BBX65 - Tsubasa's Beyblade collection.png|Tsubasa's collection of Beys. ==Trivia== *While a male in the Japanese and English dub, Tsubasa's gender was changed to female in the Korean dub for unknown reasons. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{X Characters (Season 2)}} [[Category:Anime Exclusive Characters]]

She fights with her Beyblade, [[BulletGriffon H|Rocket Griffon H]]. ==Appearance== Two Cross appears to be a tall light-skinned young woman with bluish gray eyes and waist-length icy blue hair, which is tied into twintails using hair ties shaped like an "X", falling to her hips and angular sidelocks which frame her face. She wears a navy blue unzipped hoodie with dark green crop-top that shows off her midriff and olive green trousers and black boots. ==Personality== Two has a stern and strict personality, as well as having a warrior-like view on blading, seeing it as fights displayed as strength. This is also demonstrated when she rejected Kiwami's offer for a handshake before their battle, even calling the act foolish. Despite her intimidating personality to her opponents, she does care for her youngest sister Nine, understanding that Nine has gained great allies in [[Persona|Team Persona]], though still wanting her to return to the [[Cross Corporation]]. ==Biography== ===Background=== Two is one of the nine children of Zero Cross, and the eldest daughter of the Cross family, having eight other siblings who are all talented in blading. But amongst the clan there's an open secret amongst the family of a 10th secret child whose identity is unknown. parts.title: Unique Line
parts.text:
[[File:Unique Line Logo.png|thumb|200px]]
[[File:Unique Line Expand Blade Logo.png|thumb|200px|Unique Line Expand Blade (Takara Tomy Logo)]]
[[File:UX Infinity Logo.png|thumb|200px|Unique Line Infinity (Hasbro Logo)]]
The {{Translation|'''Unique Line'''|ユニークライン|Yunīku Rain}} is the second Beyblade system of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. This line features an orange band on the packaging for its products.

For a list of parts in the '''Unique Line''' system, see [[List of Unique Line parts]].

==Structure==
{{QuotePart
|quote = Unique design, unique battle style for a competitive edge, perfect for those who want to play to their strengths!
|speaker = Official Hasbro Description}}
Like the previous [[Basic Line]] Beyblades, the Unique Line Beyblades consist of three main components: the Blade, the Ratchet, and the Bit. The main feature of Unique Line Beyblades is that metal is distributed along the outer perimeter of the Blade, creating higher Outward Weight Distribution (OWD) and greater stability. This is achieved with Launcher Hooks made of resin, rather than metal like Basic Line Beyblades.

In addition, Blades and Bits have "unique" and "one of a kind" features, hence the name of the system.

In February 2026, the '''Expand Blade''' was introduced to extend the characteristics of the UX Line by integrating the Ratchet with the Blade, further enhancing its distinctive capabilities to be possible.

===Blade===
[[File:BladeDranBuster.png|thumb|140px|DranBuster Blade]]
[[File:RatchetBladeBulletGriffon.png|thumb|140px|BulletGriffon Ratchet-Integrated Blade]]
'''Blades''' are the top component of the Bey, and act as the main contact points. The center features a "Gear Chip", showcasing a sticker of the Bey's Avatar, with a symbol indicating the spin direction. The contact points are made from zinc alloy, while the lower sections are made of PMMA.

Blades require three Launcher hooks for insertion, enabling the Bey to launch in either of the two required spin directions, whether clockwise or counterclockwise, depending on the Bey. As mentioned, the Launcher hooks are made of resin instead of metal, increasing OWD as compared to Basic Line Blades. Stoppers prevent the Bey from being spun in the wrong spin direction.

There are also Hasbro Debut Blades that use the same plastic components, but with differently designed metal components.

'''Ratchet-Intergrated Blades''' are a type of Blade which combine the Blade and Ratchet together, allowing for more in-depth and complex gimmicks.

===Ratchet===
[[File:Ratchet1-60.png|thumb|140px|1-60 Ratchet]]
'''Ratchets''' are the middle components of the Bey, attaching beneath the Blade. They vary in height and contact point design. A Ratchet attaches to the Blade by twisting, which determines the amount of Burst Resistance in each Bey. Spin direction can be changed by manually twisting the outer portion of the Ratchet, indicated by "'''L'''" or "'''R'''" spots on the Ratchet as a guide for proper assembly.

'''Simple Type Ratchets''' (Hasbro: "RBT-Ratchet") use "O-type joint", that snaps onto the Blade, rather than the standard Ratchet joints that rotate to click into place.

===Bit===
[[File:BitAccel.png|thumb|60px|Accel Bit]]
'''Bits''' act as the main contact points with the stadium floor. Most Bits have the standard 12 tooth gear that interact with the gears on the "X-Celerator Rail" ("Xtreme Line") of the [[Xtreme Stadium]], increasing the Bey's speed. Some Bits have alternate number of tooth gears that changes the speed and frequencies of Xtreme Dashes.

These are the additional subtype series of Bits aside from the standard:
*'''Low Bits,''' which are 1mm shorter
*'''High Bits,''' which are 1mm taller
*'''Gear Bits,''' which have extended teeth to catch onto the X-Celerator Rail easier
*'''Disk Bits,''' which have a outer disk that enhance its ability to produce and maintain centrifugal force
*'''Metal Bits,''' which have metal contact points
*'''Free Bits,''' which spins freely from the Ratchet
*'''Trans Bits,''' which changes the height of the Bey when performing an Xtreme Dash
*'''Bound Bits,''' which produces shock absorptions with the floor of the Xtreme Stadium
*'''Rubber Bits,''' which have rubber contact points
*'''Under Bits,''' which are 2mm shorter
*'''Wall Bits,''' which have a bumpy ring that makes contact with the floor of the Xtreme Stadium to aid the Bey in staying upright
*'''Ratchet-integrated Bit''' (Hasbro: "Combo Ratchet-Bit"), which integrates the Ratchet and Bit together

{{Product Infobox |Image=Wide Xtreme Stadium.jpeg |AKA=Wide Beystadium (Hasbro) |ProductCode=BX-32 (Takara Tomy)
G1863 (Hasbro) |ProductType=Stadium |Price=4400円

CAD$79.99 |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseJP=July 13th, 2024 |ReleaseUS=October 1st, 2025 |ReleaseCA=October 1st, 2025 |XMasters=❌ |XStandard=❌ |XOpen=✔️ }}The {{Translation|'''Wide Xtreme Stadium'''|ワイドエクストリームスタジアム|Waido Ekusutorīmu Sutajiamu}} is a stadium released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' series. It was released in Japan on July 13th, 2024 for 4400円. It later debuted in western countries as the '''Wide Beystadium''' released by [[Hasbro]] for $59.99 in the United States. ==Description== The '''Wide Xtreme Stadium''' features a wide rectangular design and "Xtreme Lines", a set of gears that interact with the gears on a Beyblade's [[Bit]] to activate the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. Bladers must launch their Beyblades at the 3 designated "Shoot Positions". There are three stadium exits in total. The two corner exits are called "Xtreme Zones" and a 3 point "Xtreme Finish" occurs when a Beyblade is knocked into these zones. On the other side is a wider center "Over Zone" and a 2 point "Over Finish" occurs when a Beyblade is knocked into this zone. Compared to the regular [[Xtreme Stadium]], the position of the zones are swapped. Introduced on July 13th, 2024, it began to be used at some [[Beyblade Battle Base]] (B4) events for the initial qualifying tournaments. Instead of 2 Bladers playing the 1on1 Battle format in the [[Xtreme Stadium]], matches were now placed between 3 Bladers in the '''Wide Xtreme Stadium''', which sped up the pace of qualifying tournaments. ===Gameplay=== The stadium can be used in two ways: in the first method of play, the "''5 Point System''", only 1 Blader can gain points per round. The last Blader standing receives the combined total of points from the 2 losing Bladers. For example, if the other two Bladers lost via Spin Finish (1 point) and Over Finish (2 points), the last Blader standing will receive 3 points total for that round. The first Blader to reach 5 points will win the match. With this first method of play, the last Blader standing can receive a minimum of 2 points (two Spin Finishes) and up to a maximum of 6 points (two Xtreme Finishes). The expected number of rounds is between 1 to 7. In the second method of play, the "''First to 2 Wins System''", if a Blader is the last Blader standing for two rounds, they win the match. The expected number of rounds is between 2 to 4. ==Dimensions== ==Gallery== ===Takara Tomy=== Wide Xtreme Stadium Packaging.jpeg|Wide Xtreme Stadium's packaging. Wide Xtreme Stadium 2.jpeg 3-Player Xtreme Stadium.png|Wide Xtreme Stadium in use. ===Hasbro=== Wide Beystadium.jpeg|Wide Beystadium Wide Beystadium Packaging.jpeg|Wide Beystadium's packaging Wide Beystadium Packaging Backside.jpeg|Backside of the Wide Beystadium's packaging. ==Videos== 【ベイブレード開発者レビュー】新レアベイ情報も！ワイドエクストリームスタジアム|Takara Tomy product overview ==Trivia== *The stadium was first unveiled via a Tweet on December 8, 2023 by the ''Beyblade X'' development team.https://twitter.com/tbh_pr/status/1733300043795538057 It later appeared at different G1 and G2 [[Beyblade Battle Base]] events.https://twitter.com/tbh_pr/status/1734442058612642029 Its original tentative name was the {{Translation|'''Xtreme Stadium for 3 Person Battles'''|3人対戦用エクストリームスタジアム|3-Ri Taisen-yō Ekusutorīmu Sutajiamu}}. **This prototype version also featured red Xtreme Lines, rather than the purple Xtreme Lines of the retail product. *This is the second Takara Tomy stadium to be released by Hasbro, after the [[Xtreme Stadium|Xtreme Stadium (Tournament Beystadium)]] released in the same year. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Beyblade X Products (Hasbro)}} [[Category:Takara Tomy]] [[Category:Hasbro]]

It debuted in Japan with the release of the BX-01 Starter, [[DranSword 3-60F]], on June 10th, 2023 for 1980円. It was later released individually by [[Hasbro]] in western countries for USD$7.99. ==Description== The '''Winder Launcher''' is a right-spin [[Ripcord Launcher]] released for the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. As the name suggests, the '''Winder Launcher''' uses a winder (ripcord) that is inserted into the launcher and then pulled out. Compared to the [[Entry Launcher (Beyblade X)|Entry Launcher]], it has a longer winder, and is compatible with accessories such as Grips and the [[Beybattle Pass]]. Takara Tomy includes the '''Winder Launcher''' in Starters and Sets, while Hasbro released it as a separate, individually packed product. ===Long Winder Launcher=== Takara Tomy's UX-14 [[ScorpioSpear 0-70Z]], CX-07/CX-00 [[PegasusBlast ATr]], and CX-09 [[SolEclipse D5-70TK]] Starters include a longer "''Long Winder''" (90 teeth compared to the standard winder's 81 and the Dragon Winder's 86), which was previously only included with the [[Hold Launcher]]. This combination of launcher and winder was originally marketed as simply "Winder Launcher + Long Winder", but supporting materials from Takara Tomy also refer to it as the "''Long Winder Launcher''".PegasusBlast Takara Tomy product overview ===Mold Variations=== At the time of writing there are three mold variations of the '''Winder Launcher''': *The original mold released by Takara Tomy at the start of the toyline in June 2023. *The second mold released by Takara Tomy in October 2023 with [[LeonClaw 5-60P]] featuring minor changes to the internals. Reprints manufactured during this period also have this mold. *The third mold released by Takara Tomy with the [[Unique Line]] Beyblades in March 2024. This mold has modified internals and uses different materials for the winder. Reprints manufactured after March 2024 also have this mold. parts.title: Xtreme Beystadium
parts.text:
{{About|the Hasbro Beyblade X stadium|Xtreme Stadium|the Takara Tomy Beyblade X stadium|5=Extreme Beystadium|6=the Metal Fight Beyblade Stadium}} {{Product Infobox |Image=Xtreme Beystadium.jpeg |ProductCode=F9588 |ProductType=Stadium |Price=USD$49.99
CAD$69.99 |Series=Beyblade X |ReleaseUS=June 1st, 2024 |ReleaseCA=May 30th, 2024 |ReleaseAU=May 16th, 2024 |XMasters=❌ |XStandard=❌ |XOpen=✔️ }}The '''Xtreme Beystadium''' is a Stadium released by [[Hasbro]] as part of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. It is the Hasbro equivalent of [[Takara Tomy]]'s [[Xtreme Stadium]], and was included with the [[Xtreme Battle Set]]. ==Description== {{QuotePart |quote = The Xtreme Beystadium arena features the X-Celerator Gear System to level-up your game. |speaker = Official Description}} The '''Xtreme Beystadium''' is the first Beystadium released by [[Hasbro]] for the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. The '''Xtreme Beystadium''' features a rectangular design and "X-Celerator Rail", a set of gears that interact with the gears on a Beyblade's [[Bit]] to activate the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. Like [[Takara Tomy]]'s [[Xtreme Stadium]], it features three Stadium pockets on one side of the stadium. The two corner pockets are called "Knockout Zones" and a 2 point "Knockout Finish" occurs when a Beyblade is knocked into these zones. The central pocket is called the "Xtreme Finish Zone" and a 3 point "Xtreme Finish" occurs when a Beyblade is knocked into it. Compared to Takara Tomy's Xtreme Stadium, the '''Xtreme Beystadium''' is shorter and rectangular rather than a square, due to the smaller dimensions. The smaller Battle Zone leads to more Xtreme Dashes and quicker battles when compared to its Takara Tomy counterpart. The reason for the smaller size is due to price point and packaging constraints.Hasbro panel at Anime NYC ==Dimensions== ==Gallery== ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Hasbro Exclusives]]

{{Special Move Infobox |Image= Xtreme Dash Max 3.png|Jaxon's Xtreme Dash Max (Multi's).png|Multi's Xtreme Dash Max.jpg|Manga |Blader=[[Jaxon Cross]]
[[Multi Nana-iro]] (manga only) |Beyblade=[[DranBrave S6-60V|Courage Dran S 6-60V]]
[[DranBrave H6-60V|Courage Dran H 6-60V]] (manga only) |Series=[[Beyblade X]] |AppearAnime=[[Beyblade X - Episode 81|All In]] |AppearManga=[[Beyblade X - Chapter 23|Messenger from the Super Summit]] }}{{Translation|'''Xtreme Dash Max'''|{{Ruby|X|エクストリーム}}ダッシュ{{Ruby|MAX|マックス}}|Ekusutorīmu Dasshu Makkusu|X-Dash Max}}, is a [[Special Move]] used by [[Jaxon Cross]] with his [[DranBrave S6-60V|Courage Dran S 6-60V]], and [[Multi Nana-iro]] with [[DranBrave H6-60V|Courage Dran H 6-60V]] in the manga. ==Description== Similar to the regular [[Xtreme Dash]], '''Xtreme Dash Max''' increases the Beyblade's speed when the gears on the Beyblade's Bit parts interact with the gears on the "X-Celerator Rail" ("Xtreme Line") of the [[Xtreme Stadium]]. With its aerodynamic shape creating a downward-directional force, Courage Dran uses its [[Assist Blade - Slash|Slash]] or [[Assist Blade - Heavy|Heavy Assist Blade]] to break the opponent's stance while the [[Main Blade - Brave|Courage Main Blade]] knocks it away, creating a ricochet effect. This special move is visualized through the 4X System with an armored Courage Dran avatar striking the opponent with a sword. ==Gallery== ===Anime=== Xtreme Dash Max 1.png Xtreme Dash Max 2.png Xtreme Dash Max 3.png Xtreme Dash Max 4.png Xtreme Dash Max 5.png ===Manga=== Xtreme Dash Max.jpg|Jaxon's Xtreme Dash Max with [[DranBrave S6-60V|Courage Dran S 6-60V]]. Xtreme Dash Max (Chapter 28).png Xtreme Dash Max (Multi's).png|Multi's Xtreme Dash Max with [[DranBrave H6-60V|Courage Dran H 6-60V]]. ==Trivia== ==References== {{X Special Moves (Season 2)}} {{X Special Moves (Season 3)}} [[Category:Beyblade X]]

'''Xtreme Dash Triple''', known as {{Translation|'''Triple Xtreme Dash'''|トリプル{{Ruby|X|エクストリーム}}ダッシュ|Toripuru Ekusutorīmu Dasshu|Triple X-Dash}} in Japan, is a [[Special Move]] used by [[Jaxon Cross]].

==Description==
<onlyinclude>Following an [[Xtreme Dash Double]], the '''Xtreme Dash Triple''' increases the Beyblade's speed when the gears on the Beyblade's Bit parts interact with the gears on the "X-Celerator Rail" ("Xtreme Line") of the [[Xtreme Stadium]] a third time, accelerating the Bey's speed to deliver another powerful hit against its opponent.</onlyinclude> 

In the anime, this Special Move is visualized through the 4X System with Dagger Dran avatar striking the opponent with three daggers.

July 15th, 2023 (Regular Release) |ReleaseUS=September 2025 |ReleaseCA=October 2025 |XMasters=✔️ |XStandard=✔️ |XOpen=✔️ }}The {{Translation|'''Xtreme Stadium'''|エクストリームスタジアム|Ekusutorīmu Sutajiamu}} is a stadium released by [[Takara Tomy]] as part of the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. It was released in Japan on June 10th, 2023 during the CoroCoro Spirit Festival. Its regular retail release in Japan was on July 15th, 2023 for 2750円. It was later released worldwide by [[Hasbro]] as the '''Tournament Beystadium'''. ==Description== {{QuotePart |quote = A stadium intended for Beyblade X. |speaker = Official Description}} The '''Xtreme Stadium''' (Hasbro: '''Tournament Beystadium''') is the first stadium released by [[Takara Tomy]] for the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' toyline. The '''Xtreme Stadium''' features a square design and "Xtreme Lines", a set of gears that interact with the gears on a Beyblade's [[Bit]] to activate the [[Xtreme Dash]] gimmick. There are three stadium exits on one side. The two corner exits are called "Over Zones" and a 2 point "Over Finish" occurs when a Beyblade is knocked into these zones. The wider, central exit is called the "Xtreme Zone" and a 3 point "Xtreme Finish" occurs when a Beyblade is knocked into it. Since its release, the '''Xtreme Stadium''' has been the tournament standard stadium for ''Beyblade X'' competitive play, and is regularly used in both [[Beyblade Battle Base]] (B4) and [[World Beyblade Organization]] (WBO) tournaments. ==Dimensions== '''Total Length:''' 43 cm '''Total Width:''' 44 cm '''Battle Zone Diameter:''' 36.5 cm '''Tornado Ridge Diameter:''' 21 cm '''Over Zone Length:''' 12 cm '''Xtreme Zone Length:''' 19 cm ==Products== ===Takara Tomy=== *BX-10 Xtreme Stadium (white, green Xtreme Line) *BX-07 [[Start Dash Set]] (Clear Ver.; black Xtreme Line) *BX-17 [[Battle Entry Set]] (Black Ver.; green Xtreme Line) *BX-53 [[All In One Set]] (Clear Black×Green; clear black with green Xtreme Line) *BX-00 Xtreme Stadium Light Package (white, red Xtreme Line) *CX-04 [[Battle Entry Set C]] (clear with pink Xtreme Line) *CX-16 [[Start Dash Set C]] (Clear×Green; clear with green Xtreme Line) *UX-04 [[Battle Entry Set U]] (Special Ver.; orange Xtreme Line) ===Hasbro=== *G0318 Tournament Beystadium (BX-10 model; white, green X-Celerator Rail) ==Gallery== ===Takara Tomy=== Xtreme Stadium Packaging.jpeg|Packaging for the Xtreme Stadium (BX-10). '''Yggdrasil Inc.''', or '''Yggdrasil Pharmaceuticals''', is a pharmaceutical company. It appears in the ''[[Beyblade X]]'' anime and manga.

In [[Beyblade X (Season 1)|Season 1]], the company would become the parent company of Mountain Ramen.

==Appearance==

==Events==
*This is where [[PhoenixFeather 3-60F|Feather Phoenix 3-60F]] was created and manufactured for mass-production.
*This is where [[PhoenixWing 9-60GF|Soar Phoenix 9-60GF]] was designed and created.
*This is where [[Blaze Fujiwara|Blaze]] and [[Khrome Ryugu|Blader Y]] battled.
*This is where [[PhoenixRudder 9-70G|Rudder Phoenix 9-70G]] was being developed.
*This is where [[Yggdrasil]]'s Beyblades Customs were created.

==Gallery==
<gallery>
</gallery>

==Trivia==
* It is presumably named after the Norse mythology of the tree known as Yggdrasil.

She fights with her ''Unicorn'' Beyblades. ==Appearance== Yuni is a tall girl with long wavy ash-blonde hair that is styled similarly to the horn and the manes of a unicorn and ringlets. She wears a teal top with long sleeves, grey shorts, black stockings with diamond-shaped holes on the left leg and round holes on the right leg, and brown boots. She also wears a pair of unicorn earrings. Her disguise outfit in [[Beyblade X - Episode 21|''Pop Production'']] also consists of her regular clothes, with a green cap and a white mask. ==Personality== ==Biography== ===Background=== ===''Beyblade X''=== ==Beyblades== *'''[[UnicornSting 5-60GP|Sting Unicorn 5-60GP]]''': Yuni's Balance Type Basic Line Beyblade in ''[[Beyblade X]]''. *'''[[UnicornSting 3-70GF|Sting Unicorn 3-70GF]]''': Yuni's Attack Type Sting Unicorn Custom in [[Beyblade X (Season 2)|''Beyblade X'']] using the [[Bit - Gear Flat|Gear Flat Bit]] as inspiration from Blaze's [[PhoenixWing 9-60GF|Soar Phoenix]]. ** It is added with the suffix "Attack Custom" in Japan. ===Decks=== ====[[Beyblade X: Xone]]==== *Sting Unicorn 5-60GP *Soar Phoenix 9-80GN *Cowl Sphinx 9-60GF ====[[Beyblade X: EvoBattle]]==== =====The X Challenge Battle===== *Sting Unicorn 3-70GF *Soar Phoenix 9-80GN *Cowl Sphinx 9-60GP =====EX Battle===== *Sting Unicorn 3-70GF *Soar Phoenix 9-60GP *Cowl Sphinx 9-80GN ===Special Moves=== *{{Special Move|Union Sting}} *{{Special Move|Unique Pass}} *{{Special Move|Xtreme Dash}} **Sting Unicorn's Xtreme Dash uses the suffix "Double Universe". Cross All-Stars |JpVoice=[[Wikipedia:Makoto Yasumura|Makoto Yasumura]] |EnVoice=[[Wikipedia:Patrick Seitz|Patrick Seitz]] |AppearAnime=[[Beyblade X - Episode 102|Another X]] |AppearManga=[[Beyblade X - Chapter 28|Futuristic Bey]] }}'''Zero Cross''', known as {{Translation|'''Zero Kurosu'''|{{Ruby|黒須|くろす}}ゼロ|Kurosu Zero}} in Japan, is the main antagonist of the third season of the anime/manga series, ''[[Beyblade X (Season 3)|Beyblade X]]''. He fights with his Beyblade, [[DrakeBrave G4-70I|Courage Drake G 4-70I]]. He is the father of the [[Cross Corporation|Cross siblings]]. ==Appearance== Zero is a tall man, His face as well as his hair and eye color is unknown. His attire consists of a grey dress shirt with a black vest over it, he also wears a metallic bodysuit with armored plating over the vest. A long white trench ocat with gold trims along the lapels with the [[Cross Corporation]] logo on the right lapel, shoulders, and chest accents, long sleeves with large turned-back cuffs with a black and yellow accents. He also wears long black pants, and grey boots. He also wears a grey with a black lens, and a light blue "0" at the center of the lens. With a white wide-brimmed fedora-style hat over the mask, and black gloves on his hands. ==Personality== Zero is shown to be laid-back and bombastic, revealing himself to Xenon City in a large hologram and sometimes singing to himself when alone. [[Robin Kazami|Robin]] even says that he's just a grown-up [[Jaxon Cross|Jaxon]]. However, he is not a good father, often not spending time with them, this led to some of his children like [[Five Cross|Five]] to be desperate to get his approval. He also allows his children to belittle each other and being emotionally manipulative to his children and using their wishes to earn his approval to get them to work harder, even dismissing them as pawns when they are no longer of use to him. ==Biography== ===Background=== Zero is the president of [[Cross Corporation]], and is the father of all nine children of the Cross family, but at some point a rumor would spread that he had a tenth child. ===''Beyblade X''=== ==Beyblades== *'''[[DrakeBrave G4-70I|Courage Drake G 4-70I]]''': Zero's Custom Line Beyblade in ''Beyblade X''. ===Special Moves=== *{{Special Move|Xtreme Dash}} **Courage Drake's Xtreme Dash uses the suffix "Dragonic Brave Next Generation". Using its [[Assist Blade - Gravity|Gravity Assist Blade]], it sends its opponent a crushing attack with its overwhelming weight. *{{Special Move|Xtreme Dash Dragonic Break Next Generation}} ==Beybattles== ===Anime=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X (Season 3) |- !Opponent !Episode !Result |- |[[Robin Kazami]] |[[Beyblade X - Episode 134|134]] |Win (3-0) |- |Robin Kazami |134 |Lose (0-2) |} ===Manga=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="width:100%" |- ! colspan="3" style="background-color:#36badf; color:white;" |Beyblade X |- !Opponent !Episode !Result |- |[[Robin Kazami]] |[[Beyblade X - Chapter 39|39]] |Win (3-0) |- |Robin Kazami |39 |Lose (0-2) |} ==Official Descriptions== The president of Cross Corporation, a company dedicated to future businesses and the father of the Cross siblings. He employs every available technology to generate flawless "future predictions". There is literally no future for Beyblade and Xenon City once he has set his sights on them. Zero Cross is a figure who brings both destruction and rebirth. In the future he envisions, the current Xenon City, The X, and Pro Bladers have no place. ==Anime Appearances== ===[[Beyblade X (Season 3)]]=== * [[Beyblade X - Episode 101|''Episode 101 - Annihilation'']] (visioned) * [[Beyblade X - Episode 102|''Episode 102 - Another X'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 103|''Episode 103 - Bey of the Future'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 104|''Episode 104 - The Wolf and the Sun'']] (flashback) * [[Beyblade X - Episode 105|''Episode 105 - A Challenge from the Future'']] (flashback) * [[Beyblade X - Episode 106|''Episode 106 - As the Super Summit'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 107|''Episode 107 - The Dyed Phoenix'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 108|''Episode 108 - X City's Savior'']] (video) * [[Beyblade X - Episode 110|''Episode 110 - The Counterattack Signal'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 112|''Episode 112 - Crafter vs. Crafter'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 113|''Episode 113 - The Phoenix's Choice'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 114|''Episode 114 - Towards the Future'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 115|''Episode 115 - Transfer or Disbandment'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 116|''Episode 116 - Future Pro'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 117|''Episode 117 - Expanding Power'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 118|''Episode 118 - Intertwining Intentions'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 119|''Episode 119 - To That Distant Place'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 120|''Episode 120 - X Tower War'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 122|''Episode 122 - The Future Beyond'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 123|''Episode 123 - One Percent of Hope'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 124|''Episode 124 - True X Tower War'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 125|''Episode 125 - The Strongest Without Desire'']] * [[Beyblade X - Episode 126|''Episode 126 - T
